docs.title: Build modular economics.
docs.text: Project Bellman is the world's first truly declarative, AI-integrated development environment for economists. It lets you build rich, dynamic heterogeneous agent models using reusable stages, focusing on economic relationships, not numerical details. Maps directly from paper to model.

docs.title: !Properties
docs.text: Expressive Any stochastic decision process can be written in the language, not only the cases a toolkit anticipated. Modular Stages written separately compose into whole models. Models grow by adding stages, not by rewriting. Declarative The specification states the economics. Solution methods are chosen separately and can be exchanged.

docs.title: About us
docs.text: Project Bellman is an Econ-ARK project for making economic models easier to express, inspect and reuse.

docs.title: 1 The project
docs.text:
Our aim is to keep an economic model understandable as it grows. In Bellman-SYM, a stage is one self-contained decision problem. Stages can be connected to form a model, while parameter values and numerical methods are specified separately.

We develop the language, its mathematical foundations and worked examples together. The model's equations and structure remain available for people and software to inspect.

Read the overview, explore a worked model, or follow the mathematical foundations.

docs.title: 2 People and support
docs.text:
The project's authors are Christopher Carroll, Alan Lujan and Akshay Shanker.

Project Bellman is part of Econ-ARK and is supported by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. Meet the wider Econ-ARK team.

docs.title: 3 Take part
docs.text:
Questions, corrections and contributions to the code, documentation and examples are welcome on GitHub. To report a problem or suggest an improvement, open an issue. For a model example, include the equations and the behaviour you expect.

The software is available under the Apache License 2.0.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: The one changelog of the project, published as the Changelog page of the documentation site. Each entry is a dated heading followed by bullets that state what changed and where; the newest entry stands first. An entry of the release names the lane whose work it records, and an entry of the work before the release names its subject. The entries of the release 0.01 stand under its heading, and the entries of the work before it under the heading "Before the release".

docs.title: 2026-11-09 — Website loading and mobile layout
docs.text:
• The homepage retains the real market and rowing footage. The opening illustration has two opposing triangles on the original ultramarine background.
  • On small screens, touch devices and with reduced motion selected, text follows the normal page layout and the videos display still images.
  • The mobile properties panel no longer shifts above its container. Decorative three-dimensional fields are hidden in the simpler layout.
  • Pages without mathematics no longer load MathJax, the equation display library. The website uses https://bellman.io/ as its canonical address.

docs.title: 2026-11-05 — Methods as components of the signature, on the calculus pages and in the wiki
docs.text:
• The Bellman calculus page Methods is written: an operator's signature carries its method and its grid as classifier components beside its inputs and outputs, each written as a typing of the operator's name, policy.method : !egm and policy.grid : !Cartesian(a=(a_min, a_max, n_a)); operators compose over their inputs and outputs alone and the labels of a composite are kept as a list; the method is a type over the kind of operator and takes keyword arguments; the grid is the discretized domain, a finite subset of the function's domain with its inclusion, over which a representation is a section; the settings a method reads are declared with their domains in the methods file and bound by configure; the handler is a binding beside the term and realizes the operator under Ρ; two erasures return the model, one forgetting the labels and one forgetting the methods file; a stage holds a declared and an operative level; nothing is differentiated. Functional programming §7 states the two erasures and the section law with the identity label on every operator without an entry, and Kinds and sorts §3 lists the grid as a sort of its own.
  • The concept wiki gains the entries grid, addition and methods, and settings is revised for the settings declared with their domains in the methods file.

docs.title: 2026-11-01 — The grid as a tagged setting
docs.text:
• A representation names its basis as the method, !Linear for piecewise linear interpolation or !pchip for the shape-preserving cubic, and its grid under settings: the grid's kind is the tag on the value of the setting grid, and the grid's fields, orders and bounds, stand beside it, settings: {grid: !Cartesian, orders: {m: n_m}, bounds: {m: [m_min, m_max]}}. !Cartesian is a kind of grid and no longer a method; it admits the fields orders and bounds, both required, and, where written, spacing and nodes. The endogenous grid method names its exogenous grid of savings the same way under its own entry, in the states of the continuation perch, orders: {a: n_a}. A representation at the policy builder's Evaluation where !egm stands writes no grid, since the knots of its interpolant are the pairs the method stores, and a representation of an authored evaluate(knots, values, x) needs none (Methodization §3; Method types).
  • Three forms are refused, each in one sentence naming the form to write or the reason: !Cartesian written as a method, orders and bounds written beside a basis or beside !egm without the setting grid, and a grid written at the policy builder's Evaluation under !egm (Refusals). A value of grid that names no kind of grid, the grid's fields written inside the tag, and the key grid written beside method are refused by the check of the options. The loader of a methods file, load_methods of bellman.stage.sources, ends a tag at a comma or a closing bracket inside a flow mapping, so that the form above written on one line is read as it is read when written over several lines.
  • configure checks the fields of a grid by their kinds, those of the exogenous grid of !egm at the states of the continuation perch, and stage.settings gives in its column grid the kind of the grid of which a setting is a field. Every methods file of the applications and of the Workbench's test models writes the tagged form: the entries that wrote !Cartesian as their method write !Linear, the piecewise linear interpolation their routines carry out, and every !egm entry names its grid of savings; buffer-stock's settings file gains n_a: 960, a_min: 0.001 and a_max: 20.0, and consumption-savings-iid and housing-owner gain a settings file for their grid of savings. The portfolio–consumption tool reads its grid of savings from the !egm entry, and the reference solution is reproduced in both orders.

docs.title: 2026-10-31 — The written place of a representation
docs.text:
• A representation method is attached to the Evaluation of a builder, and the methods file writes that place by what the Evaluation evaluates: policy.evaluate for the policy function the policy builder stores, <block-id>.evaluate.value for the value function a backward value builder writes, and <block-id>.evaluate.marginal for the derivative of that value a derivative line states, in the stage file or in a marginal block. stage.places() lists these addresses after the lines of the policy builder and of each backward value builder, of the kind operator evaluate; a solution method such as !egm stands on the builder (Methodization §2; AAS, 31 October 2026).
  • Three forms are refused, each with a sentence naming the address to write: a representation named on a builder, on: policy with !Linear; a representation named on a derivative line, on: cntn_to_dcsn.envelope; and on: evaluate in a stage that writes no evaluate(…) (Refusals). An authored evaluate(knots, values, x) keeps its address <block-id>.<statement-id>.evaluate. The value and its stated derivative share one Evaluation, which holds one representation method.
  • Every methods file of the applications and of the Workbench's test models that wrote a retired form writes the place at the Evaluation and binds the methods it bound before, except buffer-stock's. Its interpolation of consumption, bound on 31 October at the authored evaluate(m[>], c[>], m) of the method block's last line, policy.cons_choice.evaluate, is bound at the policy builder's Evaluation, policy.evaluate. The block's last line is the identification c[~] = c[>], its grid line is named g_cntn_to_dcsn, and !Linear on the arrival builder is written at dcsn_to_arvl.evaluate.value and dcsn_to_arvl.evaluate.marginal, one method for the value and its stated derivative. The pages that quote these files quote them as they now stand, and cons-port reproduces its reference in both orders. The decisions are the file MB-X of specification 0.6, with the rows marked For AAS.

docs.title: 2026-10-31 — One repository becomes three: the development repository, the public repository and the backup
docs.text:
• The repository is renamed econ-ark/bellman-dev on GitHub and stays private and whole: the toolkit, the internal folder, the team's branches and pull requests and the history since 29 December 2024. A new public repository, econ-ark/bellman, holds the toolkit alone, packages/bellman, packages/asva, packages/bellman-workbench, packages/bellman-desktop, packages/bellman-matsya-client, the applications, the documentation, the lessons and the editor extension; every commit on its main is the public subset of one development commit, written by an export script of the development repository and named in the commit message, and its first commit is a root commit. The Matsya service and the measurement harness stay in the development repository. A pull request merged on the public repository is applied to the development repository as a patch and returns in the next export. The documentation site at econ-ark.github.io/bellman is served by the public repository. Decided by AAS on 31 October 2026.
  • The root test of the repository's housekeeping keeps every exported file free of internal paths: ten test docstrings and one comment of the Workbench's editor that cited internal records by path now cite them by name, and the check of the simple-set-expressions acceptance record moved from the package's tests to a root test that only the development repository runs.
  • .githooks/pre-commit, enabled once per clone by git config core.hooksPath .githooks, refuses a staged file over 5 MB or a text that looks like a credential.

docs.title: 2026-10-31 — The buffer-stock application names its quadrature and its asset grid
docs.text:
• A methods file may hold one entry of each kind on one target, a solution method, a representation and a marginal block, since each kind has its own place; !egm on policy and !Linear on policy now stand together in one file, the second at the Evaluation that closes the policy builder (Methodization §4). The buffer-stock application writes its interpolation as an operation: the last line of its method block reads the consumption function at the resources between the candidate pairs by evaluate, and !Linear is bound on that operator occurrence, policy.cons_choice.evaluate, as the published HARK solution interpolates its consumption function; neither the decision value nor its derivative takes a representation of its own.
  • The methods file of applications/buffer-stock/ binds !gauss-hermite on the arrival builder's expectation over the two income shocks, with the node counts the new settings file names, seven for each shock, and !Linear on the stated derivative of the arrival value, D_{k}V[<], represented on the grid of 960 asset points from 0.001 to 20; the counts and the grid follow the published HARK solution of the model in the QuantEcon community library, whose equiprobable discretization and exponentially nested grid the method table does not name (Methodization §4.1; Method types).

docs.title: 2026-10-28 — One cons-port folder
docs.text:
• The portfolio–consumption model is one folder, applications/cons-port/, holding its stages written with the maximization alone, declaration/stages/{cons,disc,noport,port}/, the block files their methods files bind, declaration/methods/cons_egm.bl, port_foc.bl and noport_envelope.bl, the two recipes of its two orders with their trellis files, and the trellis files of records of its fixed reference (Model directory layout §2; Trellises §3). The demonstration folder of 21 October, applications/cons-port-demonstration/, is folded into it: its adjuster stage, bound by nothing, is removed; its tests stand under tests/, its notebook notebooks/declared-and-operative.ipynb, executed again on the derivative term of 26 October, under notebooks/. The explicit way of writing is not wanted (AAS, 28 October 2026): the stage without a portfolio choice is written the method way, its derivative line D_{k}V = E_{θ}(D_{m}V[>]*R) in a marginal block bound by !marginals; the five reference trellis files bind the folder's own stages, with the reference's handlers on the block route, and the forward law of the portfolio and no-portfolio stages carries !monte-carlo with the settings n_sim and sim_seed. applications/portfolio-choice/ stays in place, superseded and marked for deletion, its readers listed for the deletion's own step.
  • The two orders are read from the recipes: the lessons tutorials/models/cons-port/02 and 03 and tutorials/getting-started/05 call load_recipe, the Workbench's stage templates port, cons and disc come from cons-port/declaration/spec.port-cons.yml, and the documentation's API examples of a trellis file of records read trellis.port-cons-vfi.yml. The five lessons that read the folder are recorded again; the corpus recordings of its stage files stand under packages/bellman/tests/snapshot/corpus/cons-port/; the pages of the methodization, the forms catalogue, the example of the earlier YAML stages and the READMEs name the one folder.

docs.title: 2026-10-28 — The applications are written the method way, and the trivial arrival builders go
docs.text:
• Every application's stage file states its values and its maximizations alone. A derivative line stands in a marginal block of a block file under declaration/methods/, bound on the value builder by an entry method: !marginals whose block names the file from the methods file's folder, ../../methods/<file> from a per-stage methods file; the inverse Euler, endogenous-grid, candidate-value and upper-envelope lines stand in a method block bound on the policy builder by !egm, and a first-order condition in one bound by !time-iteration. Line ids are kept, so a representation bound on a derivative line's id keeps its address. Rewritten so: buffer-stock, retirement-choice, consumption-savings-iid, benhabib-2019, housing-renting, pension-retirement, durables, housing-frictions and housing-owner.
  • The degenerate arrival builders, a forward builder whose only lines are identities between the arrival states and the decision states and a backward builder writing V[<] = V, are removed from the stages that had them; such a stage is entered at its decision perch, and a connector of a period or a trellis names its decision states. A terminal stage whose states are typed in its arrival block alone keeps it, and cagetti-denardi-2006 keeps its arrival builders, which its branching connectors name.
  • The package: a method block may call upper_env and evaluate; a !marginals entry may share its builder with another method's entry; a maximization binder is in scope in the feasible sets written after it; the model explorer draws reading ports at a stage's entry perch; three refusal examples follow the moved lines of consumption-savings-iid.
  • The cons-port demonstration's portfolio stage names its continuation state w in place of m_next, and portfolio-choice's block file moves to applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/methods/, since the test corpus reads every .bl file under declaration/stages/ as a stage file.
  • The pages and the lessons that quote these files quote them as they now stand. The decisions are the files MB-R, MB-S, MB-U and MB-V of specification 0.6, with the rows marked For AAS: the entry perch's typing where a stage has no forward block, the connector list of a trellis admitting no default, and the Workbench's remaining reads of the arrival perch.

docs.title: 2026-10-26 — Matsya's composer is a text area sized by its text or by a handle
docs.text:
• The field of the Matsya column's composer is a text area: Enter sends the question, Shift+Enter begins a new line, text pasted into it keeps its line breaks, and a question of several lines is listed with its breaks. Empty, the field is one line of 26 px with the line centered in it; it grows with its text by 18 px a line to eight lines, 152 px, and then scrolls (The Workbench §5).
  • The top edge of the composer's box is a handle: a drag upward enlarges the field while the conversation gives up the space down to 80 px, a drag downward stops at one line, a double click returns the field to the height of its text, and the browser keeps the height dragged with the window's other sizes for the folder, writing nothing in the model folder. Escape in the field moves the focus to the conversation and keeps the text; Enter that confirms an input method's candidate sends nothing.
  • Built on 26 October 2026 on the branch amd-07/composer under amendment 07 of model interface specification 0.4, AI/build-areas/model-interface/spec_0.4/amendments/amd-07-the-composer-of-the-matsya-column.md, merge pending AAS: field.vue's property grows, the handle composer of window.vue, the composer of matsya_window.py and its rules in brand.css; the tests read the composer as a text area again, and packages/bellman-workbench/tests/test_amd_07.py checks the amendment's six cases. The record is AI/operations/verification/model-interface/2026-10-26-amd-07/report.md and the decisions AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/model-interface-decisions-made-by-ai/amd-07-the-composer-decisions.md.

docs.title: 2026-10-26 — The value wire carries its derivatives
docs.text:
• A marginal value is no longer a field of a backward header or a wire of the builders graph. The derivative of a value is read where a line needs it by the derivative term D_{a}V[>], the operator D applied to the value field written with its perch mark, the subscript a state coordinate of the perch at which the value is read, written without its mark; a backward header lists value fields and the controls at which its lines are read, and nothing else. The roles !mrgnvl and !sndmrgnvl, the naming convention dV, d_<coordinate><value> and the refusal marginal-value-pairing are retired, and a header that writes a retired role word is refused with a sentence naming the term (Stages; Field equations §2; Expression forms; Refusals).
  • A derivative line, D_{m_d}V = 𝑑𝑢(c), in a value builder's block of the stage file or in a marginal block bound with !marginals, states the derivative of the value the builder writes. methodize records it at the builder's Evaluation beside the representation method, by coordinate with its id and source; the graph gains no wire and no box, the builder's signature is unchanged, the value's record lists the coordinate under derivatives, and stage.obligations() lists the reading under marginal-reading. How a derivative is evaluated is a property of the value fixed where it is built, by the stated line, by the value's representation, or by a representation of the stated derivative bound on the derivative line's id, on: cntn_to_dcsn.envelope; a block that reads D_{a}V[>] declares nothing about it. No derivative line is written on an arrival builder whose law between the perches is the identity, where the stored derivative values pass through; where the law is not the identity, the author writes the arrival derivative line with the law's factor (Methodization §4.1).
  • The method table loses the column "reads a marginal value" and gains derivatives it evaluates, stated for !Linear, !Cartesian and !pchip, and the condition marginal-reading of !marginals reads as the derivative line's assertion under the envelope conditions (Method types). bellman.trellis.derivative_missing(trellis) replaces marginal_missing and answers one derivative-missing diagnostic for each derivative reading no route meets, naming the stage, the value and the coordinate; the join check compares value fields alone (Trellises §2.1). A row that reads a derivative term compiles to no kernel and is refused under kernel-form.
  • The explicit way of writing stays, with derivative terms in place of marginal fields, and a stage file may define dV = D_{a}V[>] and read the name. The canonical example, applications/cons-port-demonstration/, writes its states unindexed by perch, m at the decision perch, and declares no arrival perch: its decision value is the value the stage exports, and the trellis joins the stage before it at its decision state. The Bellman Workbench draws a value as one wire, whose port's hover lists the derivatives the value carries, prints the stated derivative on a card at the Evaluation beside the representation, and shows derivative-missing under the Problems mark (The Workbench). The pages of the documentation, the catalogues of the calculus and the example pages state the amended language.
  • Matsya's configuration 0.3.32, ID fe160391c16327681b3f564f423898ead4254f47331eed7985c2095568603356, revises the instruction texts of the Bellman-SYM writer, the source preparer, the paper-form reader and the typed-form writer for the derivative term in place of the marginal field and regenerates the three saved guides from the pages of this entry; the Matsya handler, the settings and the retrieval index are unchanged.
  • Built on 26 October 2026 by the units of the plan AI/build-areas/Bellman-Sym/spec_0.6/2026-10-26-amd-mb-001-implementation-plan.md, the language, methodization and the trellis, the applications, the pages and the Workbench, Matsya's texts and guides, and the tests, and merged into main the same day by the merge commit that carries this entry; the cons-port demonstration reproduces its reference in both orders to 1e-13, and the Workbench draws its consumption stage with values alone and its operative builders with the stated derivative at the Evaluation. The retrieval index is not rebuilt and the writer job of the amendment's item 6 is not run; both wait for AAS.

docs.title: 2026-10-22 — The Workbench finds the Matsya client in its own environment

docs.title: 2026-10-22 — Matsya configuration 0.3.31 for method blocks and marginal blocks (specification 0.6, unit H)
docs.text: • The configuration 0.3.31, ID 16bcb5781bab092101e94551e290282e853c9f996946493d41485d3de4f9617c, regenerates the three saved guides from the published pages of the merged build of specification 0.6, so that the writer's pages hold the method block and the marginal block of a block file, the key block, the method !marginals, the methods page's columns and the trellis page's marginal value a method reads. Its writer text texts/BellmanStageProse-to-BellmanSYMDeclaration.md states that a policy block writes the maximization alone where the description states the policy by its maximization, also where the description computes it by the endogenous grid method, and the explicit way with the Euler equation where the description states that equation; it states the keys of a methods entry, and that the files of a job hold no block file, so that the writer writes no block key and names in the note a method that needs one. The preparer text texts/SourceMaterial-to-BellmanStageProse.md states the maximization as the condition that determines the policy where the source computes it by a method. The distribution check, the Matsya handler, the settings and the retrieval index are unchanged; publication on the service and the default are separate steps (AI/operations/matsya/configuration-revisions/register.md).

docs.title: 2026-10-22 — The specification 0.6 build installed on the Matsya service
docs.text: • The Bellman Matsya service runs Bellman 0.1.6, meaning-map-training 0.1.9 and bellman-matsya 0.1.13, built from the merged build of specification 0.6 and installed in place with the job database kept; the index answer names the service's version and its capabilities capture_at_acceptance and job_delivery_id. Configuration 0.3.31, whose guides and texts describe method blocks and marginal blocks, is published; the default configuration stays 0.3.20.

docs.title: 2026-10-22 — Method blocks and marginal blocks
docs.text:
• A methods file may name a block file under the new key block, a path from the methods file's folder, and methodize reads it. A method block, whose header carries the signature of a builder of the stage, becomes that builder's operations, as the block of !egm does on the policy builder of a stage file that writes the maximization alone; a marginal block, bound by the new method !marginals on a backward value builder, appends the author's marginal lines to that builder, whose Evaluation then writes the marginal value beside the value. Nothing is differentiated, and the stage file is not changed (Methodization §4.1; Expression forms §4).
  • The binding verbs calibrate, methodize and configure add their binding to the stage they are called on and return it; nothing is copied. stage.declared reads the builders as the stage file states them and stage.builder the operative ones, the same builders until a block is bound, and the initial diagrams and the declared builders are the same objects before and after every binding. A target holds one binding of each kind, a solution method, a representation or a marginal block, and a later binding of a kind replaces the earlier (The binding verbs).
  • Each method type of the package's method table states whether it takes a block, whether it reads a marginal value, and the condition its construction requires, which stage.obligations() lists and nothing checks, egm-eligibility for !egm and marginal-reading for !marginals. !time-iteration takes a block and reads a marginal value, and !vfi reads the setting n_c, the number of points of the finite feasible set its search uses (Method types).
  • bellman.trellis.marginal_missing(trellis) reports a marginal value that a method reads and the stage supplying the continuation does not export, as a marginal-missing diagnostic naming the stage and the field; nothing is refused (Trellises §2.1).
  • A block file stands at declaration/methods/<name>.bl of a model folder (Model directory layout §4). The folder applications/cons-port-demonstration/ binds the consumption stage's block file cons_egm.bl and the portfolio stage's port_foc.bl in both orders of its trellis.
  • The encoding schema admits the key block in a method entry, so that the encoding of a stage bound with a block file passes validate_encoding. The notebook applications/cons-port-demonstration/notebooks/declared-and-operative.ipynb shows the declared and the operative builders of the demonstration's two stages, and the marginal value each order of its trellis requires, met and then unmet.
  • The demonstration applications/cons-port-demonstration/ writes the consumption and portfolio stages with their maximization alone and binds the endogenous grid method as a method block, with the marginal utility and its inverse written in closed form in the block file; its two orders, consumption first and portfolio first, reproduce the cons-port reference to 1e-12 (tests/test_reference_solve.py). The cons-port application's own recipes bind that consumption stage, and lessons 01, 03 and 04 of the cons-port tutorials are recorded again on it.
  • Bellman Workbench: the button Operative builders at the foot of a stage's graph, beside Perch overlays, switches the builders shown and the sections of Details between the declared builders and the builders a method opens, off when a folder opens (design pass 15, Workbench); a node names every method its box holds.
  • Bellman Workbench: the Matsya column stands on the page's ground behind one hairline, with a composer box of context chips, the text field and a foot row holding the kind of request, its output level or collection and the send control (design pass 16); a question from a connected folder is a turn of its project session, a build shows its prepared material before it is sent and its result in five parts, citations open their file and line, their saved copy or their passage, and returned files are downloaded into keyed copies, inspected read-only under their own root and adopted through a recorded, recoverable plan (amendment 06 of the model-interface specification).
  • The client bellman-matsya sends a delivery identifier with job submit-prepared, refuses one longer than 64 characters with a sentence, and the user-guide pages 04 and 05 describe reviewed_through, the capabilities and the new commands.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — Matsya fixes a job's source material at acceptance, and the client's four additions (specification 0.6, unit G1)
docs.text:
• A job from a session may name reviewed_through, the number of the last session entry its user reviewed. The job store checks the session in the transaction that accepts the job: entries after that number refuse it with 409 and a sentence naming each entry by its number and kind, a number beyond the last entry refuses it with 422, and neither creates a job. Otherwise the store fixes the job's source material, its kind, the revision, the entries' numbers and the earlier job it continues, the session's latest job at acceptance; the worker reads them in place of the session and passes that earlier job's record to the processor, so that neither an entry added nor a job ended while the job waits changes what it reads; the job's answer names reviewed_through; and the record names the history it was built from under captured_source, which the products view keeps (packages/matsya/matsya_service/jobs.py, check_reviewed_history; processor.py, check_request). A job submitted without the field is built as before. A job request may name a delivery_id: the same request sent again under it returns the job held, its present state and repeated true, and creates nothing, and a different request under it is refused with 409. A repeated delivery_id on a reply or a turn already returned the entry or the turn held, with no scheduled value and no new work (AMD-MAT-006 §8 rule 3), and is unchanged.
  • The migration adds to the jobs table the columns reviewed_through INTEGER, captured_source TEXT, continues_job TEXT and delivery_id TEXT, with an index that keeps a delivery_id unique among one principal's jobs, NULL in every row written before it, so that every earlier job reads as a job submitted without either field; no other table changes, and the record schemas matsya-model-iteration/7 and /6 are unchanged, captured_source being an optional entry of a captured job's record. The answer of GET /v1/index names capabilities, ["capture_at_acceptance", "job_delivery_id"], and service_version, so that a client claims either only of a service that names it. The Matsya service is version 0.1.13. A client released before this change sends no reviewed_through, and every answer it reads keeps its fields.
  • The client bellman-matsya is version 0.13.0: job submit-prepared <file> [--delivery-id ID] submits a job from a prepared-inputs file (the session, the last entry reviewed, the target, the starting declaration as submit_job takes it and each file's path in the model folder; bellman_matsya.client.read_prepared_inputs defines it) and is refused, before the job request, by a service whose index answer does not name the capability; configuration effective prints the service address, the configuration, the session and the sources of the Matsya token and the personal key, without either secret, and reports a key the client does not send to the address as refused; ask --no-wait prints a turn's identifier at once and ask --delivery-id names its delivery; and turn status and turn wait read a turn by its identifier from any later process (packages/bellman-matsya-client/src/bellman_matsya/).
  • Built and tested locally on the branch spec06/matsya-service (packages/matsya/tests/test_spec_0_6_unit_g1.py, packages/bellman-matsya-client/tests/test_spec_0_6_unit_g1_client.py; decisions in AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/spec-06-decisions-made-by-ai/SG1-unit-g1-the-service-and-the-client.md). The installed service on DigitalOcean is unchanged; installing 0.1.13 there is a separate operation.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — Bellman Workbench: one line per bundle, the vertical layout, and the trellis's Initial view (design pass 14)
docs.text: • Design pass 14 (AI/operations/verification/model-interface/2026-10-21-design-pass-14/design-pass-14-one-line-per-bundle.md), after AAS's words of 21 October 2026 on the page merged as unit Q, in ten rules, built as unit S on codex/model-interface-s. In a stage's builders graph the wires that carry a value and its marginal values from one box to another are one line with the count of its wires at its plug, as the trellis draws a cable, the port of its first wire at each end, whose hover lists the wires drawn at it, and its wires' labels in its own hover; a measure, a control or a field wire stays a line of its own. Every graph opens laid out from top to bottom, and the direction turned with the foot button holds for every graph of every stage and of the trellis while the page is open and is remembered by the browser under bellman-workbench layout; the automatic turn of a wide field diagram is withdrawn. Laid out downward, the markers of one side of a period frame stand apart by their widest label and 8 px, so that no label runs over another. An unnamed result wire is spelled without its mark :result wherever the package prints an expression or a type, dcsn_to_arvl.value:Expectation:1, the identities and the ids unchanged; six stage snapshots are recorded again for that spelling alone. Matsya's composer is a text field of one line at the page's control height, its text and its button Ask on one axis, its empty words Matsya query?. The trellis offers the select Graph as a stage's view does: Initial shows the trellis's initial diagram of the direction, each occurrence's fields in their perch layers with its blocks, and every connection drawn as a wire from the field it reads to the field it supplies, carrying the route's record; the view is read, not written; the two diagrams are computed when Initial is chosen and kept while the view shows one of them, since those of a long trellis are large (S-D30). The add glyph beside Stage and Period is 12 px on the word's cap height. A card's strip segment is orange for the builder that joins the continuation perch and mint for the one that joins the arrival perch, the policy's tint of ice kept. The toggles of Files and Inspector stand at the left end of the main bar after Forward, where those regions open, and those of Details and Matsya at the right after Go to. The decisions are in AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/model-interface-decisions-made-by-ai/model-interface-s-decisions.md; the package's test suites test_behaviour.py, test_snapshot.py and cat/test_model_explorer.py fail at main before this unit (101 failures and 28 errors at b3df18733, the methods binding of cons.bl refused), which the unit records as S-D17 and does not repair. Merged into main on 21 October 2026 after the delegated acceptance (AI/build-areas/model-interface/spec_0.4/reviews/2026-10-21-unit-s-delegated-acceptance.md); the fix wave of the same day repaired the Problems mark, which emptied the page of a model whose backward graph is refused by asking the package for the joins of the trellis's initial diagram (S-D22), and gave Details the nodes of the trellis's Initial view (S-D21).

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — The comparator integrates a uniform law
docs.text: • The comparator of packages/meaning-map-training integrates Uniform(a, b) by Gauss–Legendre nodes on [a, b], the weights summing to one and a polynomial of the draw exact up to degree 2n − 1 at n nodes, so that an expectation over a uniform shock is evaluated at its test points as one over a normal or a lognormal shock is; endpoints equal, reversed or infinite are refused as outside the domain, and TruncatedNormal and TypeIExtremeValue are still not integrated (compare.py, _Evaluator.law_nodes). CDC asked for it on 20 October 2026, after the cross-toolkit schemas' converter wrote Uniform(0.6, 1.4) and the comparator reported the law not integrated. The list of law families the comparator keeps apart from the names of a stage now names Uniform, TruncatedNormal and TypeIExtremeValue, the families of pull request 17, as the package's table of families does. Tests: tests/test_stage_compare.py, the uniform's nodes and moments, an identity that holds under a declared uniform law only, and a pair that differs by the family.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — The comparator evaluates finite index sets, indexed data and category codes
docs.text:
• The comparator of the meaning-map training evaluates at its test points the kernels that read the forms of pull requests 14 and 16, which it did not evaluate before, so that two writings differing in such a kernel, dist[i_d][j] for dist[j][i_d], ended undecided and not differ (packages/meaning-map-training/meaning_map_training/compare.py, _draw and the functions it calls). A name declared on an integer range, i : {1, …, J}, is drawn as an integer between the bounds of the range at the point, a parameter that a bound reads, J, being drawn first from its own declared set where the point lacks it; a name declared on a listed set, {0, θ} ⊂ ℤ, takes one of its members; and a name declared on a comprehension over the integers, the category-coded {i : ℤ | i >= 0, i <= 1}, takes an integer between the bounds its conditions write, drawn again until every condition holds, so that the code 0 is drawn as well as the code 1.
  • A name declared on a set of functions, δ : L_J → ℝ or dist : L_J × L_J → ℝ₊, is drawn as a table with one entry drawn from the codomain for each member of the index set, each entry drawn on its own, so that a table on pairs is in general not symmetric; the table on a product is nested by its factors, and a table on a set of labels is keyed by the positions at which a field on that set is drawn. The selections δ[j] and dist[j][i_d] read the entry at the integer key nearest the selector, a missing key making the point invalid; the selection from a tuple is unchanged (_Evaluator.value). A table whose index set cannot be listed at a point, among them a listed set whose parameter member is drawn as no integer, makes the point invalid for a statement that reads it and is left out of the point for a statement that does not (_points). A table lies in its set of functions and in no other set (_within), and a witness writes a drawn table with its keys as text (_rounded).
  • The items print the three set forms as a stage file spells them, {1, …, J}, L_J × L_J → ℝ₊ and {0, θ} ⊂ ℤ, where before they printed the fields of the term, IntegerRange(lower=1, upper=J) (packages/meaning-map-training/meaning_map_training/items.py, term_text).
  • Six tests of packages/meaning-map-training/tests/test_stage_compare.py check the change on the location stage of packages/bellman/tests/test_finite_indexed_data.py with J : ℤ, >= 1, on its writing with the outside option I_J := {0, …, J}, on the household stage of packages/bellman/tests/test_category_codes.py and on the stage with listed integer keys; at the base b3df18733 five of them fail, four ending undecided where differ is required and one on the printed text. The harness suite gives 510 passed and 36 skipped, with one failure that stands at the base, test_round_trip.py::test_anonymise_hides_the_name_and_the_path_of_the_portfolio_cons_dossier, whose stage file of commit a8b484899 the compiler now refuses under input-perch-state. The 80 stage files that elaborate under applications/, packages/bellman/tests/corpus/ and the harness's fixtures, each compared with itself and with its mutations, 918 comparisons in all, give the same profiles as at the base. An expectation over a shock with one of the three laws of pull request 17 is still not evaluated, since the quadrature integrates the normal and lognormal laws and their mixtures only.
  • The package meaning-map-training is version 0.1.8, and the Matsya service is 0.1.12 and requires it. mutate.py, the round-trip programs and the Bellman package are unchanged.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — The proposer's classification rule
docs.text: • The configuration proposer of the meaning-map training (AI/operations/meaning-map-training/epoch-template/proposer-instructions.md) calls a form a fault of the language only where a refusal of the pass, classified language, met it and no admitted spelling of the same mathematics stands in the documentation, in applications/ or in the pass's own files; a writer's note naming a missing construct, or a preparer's description calling a stage a branching stage, is a claim to check. The branching clause of item 1 and item 3 of the forms the meaning-map training found missing had entered that list without such a refusal (AAS, 21 October 2026). The rule applies from the next epoch's copy of the text; no epoch in progress is changed.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — Matsya configuration 0.3.30 for the October builds
docs.text: • The configuration 0.3.30, ID 55e3d1c5cec4d496ed6d7d0e5fa804180bcdadef7a4a81b5cc5b8aec0677135c, regenerates the three saved guides from the published pages at commit 8a55aaad9, so that the writer's pages hold the finite index sets, the category codes, the ten shock families and the rule that alternatives with one successor stage are one block with an integer state. Its writer text texts/BellmanStageProse-to-BellmanSYMDeclaration.md states that form of a choice among J alternatives, prescribes for a branch on which the model ends the retained state and a listed continuation value that the user supplies, zero where the description gives no bequest value, in place of the field joined to nothing of 0.3.29, lists the ten families with the spellings of the three new ones, and no longer names the type-I extreme-value law among the constructs the language lacks; the preparer text and the distribution check name the ten families. The test fixture's copy of the texts and the version assertion are brought to 0.3.30, and the 399 service tests pass. The handler, the settings and the retrieval index are unchanged (AI/operations/matsya/configuration/README.md). It was published to the service at 01:29 UTC on 21 October 2026 as a registered alternative, the default staying 0.3.20 (AI/operations/matsya/configuration-revisions/register.md).

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — One block for alternatives with one successor, and the death branch's value
docs.text: • Branching §1 and Stages §2.1 state that alternatives which all lead to the same successor stage are not branches: the choice is an integer control over the index set, and one block retains the chosen alternative as the integer continuation state, i_n = j, so that the number of alternatives stays a parameter; an alternative with a continuation problem of its own is a branch of a separate stage. Branching §4 states that a branch on which the model ends keeps the state its terminal value reads, and that the stage supplying that value lists V[>], which the user supplies at realization, zero where the paper gives no bequest value (AAS, 21 October 2026). No compiler code changed.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 Terminal continuation values
docs.text: • Trellis Syntax states that a terminal stage retains an explicit continuation-value input. The user supplies its value function, including zero where appropriate; a terminal date or death branch supplies no automatic zero value. This clarification changes no compiler code.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 — Continuous shock distributions marked done
docs.text: • AAS marked the brief additional-continuous-shock-distributions.md done on 21 October 2026, and with it item 5(a) and the extreme-value law of item 1 of the forms the meaning-map training found missing (AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/bellman-sym-forms-the-meaning-map-training-found-missing.md); the specification 0.5 index and its status row record the same, and the issue stays open for its remaining forms. The package is unchanged.

docs.title: 2026-10-20 — The truncated lognormal law, and the condition law-support
docs.text:
• A shock's distribution may be declared by TruncatedLogNormal(μ, σ, l, u): the lognormal law whose logarithm has mean μ and standard deviation σ > 0, conditional on the interval [l, u] of the draw itself, with 0 ≤ l < u, 0 for no lower bound and inf for no upper, so that TruncatedLogNormal(μ, σ, 0, inf) is LogNormal(μ, σ) (Shock distributions). CDC requested the family on 18 October 2026 for the cross-toolkit schemas and on 20 October spelled it as TruncatedNormal(μ, σ, l, u) is spelled, location first, the endpoints in the draw's units and no defaults; the schemas' convention, bounds in standard deviations of the logarithm and a mean pinned at one, is a conversion a file's writer makes, exp(μ + k·σ) for a bound of k standard deviations. The family is the fourth real-parameter family of distributions/families.py, so its arguments are checked, retained as distribution-parameters-in-domain where they name parameters, and admitted as a mixture's component and on a collection subject as the other three are.
  • The family has a definition in the table of definitions, a probability measure on (0, ∞): the standard normal density integrated over the z with exp(μ + σ·z) in the event and in [l, u], divided by its integral over the z with exp(μ + σ·z) in [l, u], the normalizing mass a symbolic denominator as the truncated normal's is. A declaration denotes the law as written and its measure at the written arguments, and its forward and backward builders are constructed; a truncated component of a Mixture is pushed forward from (0, ∞) into ℝ as a lognormal component is.
  • Refused under distribution-domain at the declaration: σ zero or negative, a negative lower endpoint, -inf included, since the draw is positive, endpoints equal, reversed or both infinite, an infinite μ or σ and a tuple argument; a call of another number of arguments under readable-form.
  • The condition law-support-and-provider is renamed law-support, "The distribution of ψ gives probability only to values in the declared shock set": the numerical routine that provides a law to a solver is no condition of the stage (CDC, 19 October 2026). calibrate decides the condition where the package knows the law's support and reads the bounds of the declared set, which it does for the truncated lognormal, whose support is [l, u], open at a lower endpoint 0 and at an upper endpoint inf: established with the values and the support as evidence, or the calibration refused when the support lies outside the set; for every other family it stays required (stage/binding_verbs.py, calibrated_supports; distributions/families.py, law_support).
  • The encoding schema admits the primitive TruncatedLogNormal; the comparator of packages/meaning-map-training lists the family and integrates it by the lognormal's Gauss–Hermite nodes where every node lies in the window [(ln l − μ)/σ, (ln u − μ)/σ], and otherwise by Gauss–Legendre nodes in the standard-normal variable over the window, weighted by the normal density; distributions/truncation.py holds the window, the normal mass of it and the support. The word lists of the Workbench's editor bundle and of the VS Code grammar name the four real-parameter families and Categorical.
  • Tests: tests/test_amd_sg_036.py, one test per acceptance item of AMD-SG-036; the family's list in tests/test_continuous_distributions.py; a pair of laws in the comparator's test_stage_compare.py. The recording retiree_death is re-recorded for the renamed condition and the family list of its not-constructed message; the stored corpus encodings and the two death stages' notes carry the new name and the eleven families by text. Documentation: Shock distributions, whose table, the laws row of Forms and Operations are written again by docs/_hooks/reference_pages.py.

docs.title: 2026-10-20 — Additional continuous shock distributions
docs.text:
• A shock's distribution may be declared by three more families: Uniform(a, b), the uniform law on [a, b] with finite a < b; TruncatedNormal(μ, σ, l, u), the normal law of mean μ and standard deviation σ > 0 conditional on [l, u], with extended-real endpoints l < u, -inf and inf admitted; and TypeIExtremeValue(μ, s), the maximum type-I extreme-value law of location μ and scale s > 0, whose cumulative distribution is exp(−exp(−(x − μ)/s)) (distributions/families.py, FAMILY_ARGUMENTS; Shock distributions). AAS requested the three together, for items 1 and 5(a) of the forms the meaning-map training found missing (AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/bellman-sym-forms-the-meaning-map-training-found-missing.md); the parameter conventions and the checks are decisions of the brief additional-continuous-shock-distributions.md, not rulings of AAS.
  • Each family has a definition in the table of definitions, a measure on ℝ written with the real exponential and the Lebesgue measure and with no function the package does not define: the density 1/(b − a) on [a, b]; the standard normal density integrated over the part of the event in [l, u], divided by its integral over [l, u], so that the normalizing mass stands as a symbolic denominator and nothing is clipped or censored; and the density exp(−z − exp(−z)) of the standardized draw z = (x − μ)/s. A positive scale is the domain (0, ∞) of the definition's variable, and the orders a < b and l < u are requirements of the definitions under distribution-parameters-in-domain (typing/primitive_definitions.py). N, LogNormal and TruncatedNormal share one standard normal density.
  • A declaration of one real shock by N, LogNormal or one of the three denotes two objects: the law as written and its measure at the written arguments, the family's definition with the arguments in place of its variables, a bound letter of the definition primed where a written argument, or the name a conditional law is a function of, ν in P_{Ψ|ν}, is spelled the same, z′ for y ~ N(z, 1). definition_measure of stage/defining_expressions.py gives the measure, _distribution_denoted of stage/denotations.py answers it as a second Denoted under the symbol P_y, or P_{Ψ|ν} for a law conditional on ν, and the card prints it on the row under the law, P_y = measure on ℝ given by B ↦ … (display/cards.py; The definitions table). The declarations of N and LogNormal gain the row; the cards of the expectations and distribution extensions that read a declaration print the law as written alone, and the supporting definitions of every other record list the declaration by its law alone; a Mixture, a tuple subject and the other families denote one object as before.
  • A call of LogNormal or of one of the three with real arguments, declared for a shock on the functions from a finite index set, ε : I_J → ℝ, is the law of each component, and the declaration denotes the finite product of that law over the index set, printed ⊗_{i ∈ I_J} TypeIExtremeValue(0, 1): the probability measure on the functions e from I_J to ℝ whose value at the set of the e with e(i) in B_i for every i is the product of the components' probabilities of the B_i. The product is the new semantic constructor ProductMeasure(binding binding, expr body), whose binding's domain lies outside its scope and whose body may read the index, parents and parameters but no other component (syntax/grammars/semantic.asdl; typing/typed_expressions.py, regenerated by gen_semantic_types.py, with its binding, substitution, comparison and printing). The measure of such a declaration is the product of the scalar measures, and the sentence of joint-distribution-factorization adds the components of ε are independent, each with the law TypeIExtremeValue(0, 1), or conditionally independent given η for ε ~ TypeIExtremeValue(η, 1) (distributions/edges.py, factorization_obligation). A scalar LogNormal on such a shock, admitted before without a product meaning, takes the product. N there is the joint normal law of the components as before, and a scalar N(0, 1) there is still refused at calibration; a Mixture there is not a product. An expectation that integrates a parent inside an expectation conditioned on the indexed shock is refused under conditional-not-declared, as any posterior is.
  • Elaboration, and calibration where an argument names a parameter, refuse under distribution-domain, at the declaration's file position, the arguments of the three outside their domains: endpoints not in order, Uniform(1, 1) and TruncatedNormal(0, 1, inf, inf) among them; a standard deviation or a scale that is not positive; an infinite argument other than an endpoint of a truncation; an argument whose names all have values and whose arithmetic has no number, 0/0, or is not a number, inf - inf; a tuple argument; a parameter declared on a collection, μ : I_J → ℝ, or on a product set, b : ℝ × ℝ; and a tuple subject (distributions/families.py, check_family_conditions and check_real_parameter_shapes; fold/stage_fold.py, _distribution_obligations). Every component of a Mixture that is a call of N, LogNormal or one of the three is checked as its declaration would be, and the refusal names the component, so that Mixture((0.5, 0), (0.5, N(0, -1))), admitted before, is refused. The package computes no normalizing mass, and TruncatedNormal(0, 1, 9, 10), whose mass is about 1.13 · 10⁻¹⁹, is admitted. The claim of the rule in refusals.py names the new conditions, and so does its row on Refusals.
  • An argument of the three that reads a parameter without a value keeps the family's condition as the new obligation distribution-parameters-in-domain of refusals.CONDITIONS, decided at calibration. A declaration has one such obligation, holding the clause of each of its components, and its sentence states the condition in the written terms: the parameters of the Uniform declaration two_nodes:distribution:y of y lie in the family's domain: a < b, with a = a_y and b = b_y, both finite. A condition of N or LogNormal that reads a parameter is decided at calibration as before and is not listed, and a mixture keeps its obligation distribution-weights-are-a-probability-vector.
  • An encoded answer writes the product as a node semantic.ProductMeasure with one binding, the binding's domain and one body; the schema stage-encoding/2.6 is extended in place with the kind, its fields and the three family names among the primitive names, as it was for records.CategoryCodes (display/answer_encoding.py; display/encoding_checks.py; display/stage-encoding-2.6.schema.json).
  • The kernel lines of an expectation or a distribution extension write a component of a mixture as a point mass only where the component is a number; before, the last argument of TruncatedNormal(0, 1, -1, 1) inside a mixture would have been written point mass at 1 (stage/kernels.py, _point_masses).
  • The forward and backward builders of a stage that declares one of the three are constructed, and a period of two such stages certifies its connection. No routine for integration, sampling or optimization is added: a numerical routine must provide the distribution, the condition law-support-and-provider that every declaration records. The checks of undefined arithmetic and of NaN are made for the three families alone, so that N(0/0, 1) is still admitted. Symbolic branching, log-sum choice formulas, piecewise functions and terminal stages, which Almagro's model also needs, are not part of this change.
  • The tests are packages/bellman/tests/test_continuous_distributions.py, with one test for each of the brief's acceptance items 1 to 6, 28 cases in all, of which the file's first version failed 24 of its 26 at the base b047e23fe, the sixth checking the executed notebook of the verification folder 2026-10-20-continuous-distributions; test_behaviour.py's test of a declared law reads the second object of ψ ~ LogNormal(-(σ_ψ^2)/2, σ_ψ). Documentation: Shock distributions, the laws row of Forms, the distribution-domain row of Refusals and the card section of The definitions table.
  • The parsed terms of the 638 stage files of the repository are unchanged, and of the 48 under applications/ the 42 that elaborate print the same stage cards, their definitions cards differing only on the rows of their scalar N and LogNormal declarations. Of the recordings under packages/bellman/tests/snapshot/, ez_savings, sa_savings and tenure are re-recorded for the second denoted object of those declarations and retiree_death for the family list of its not-constructed message; cons, which differs from its recording since 16 October, is left as it stands. The corpus encodings of buffer_stock, tenure, ez_savings and worker_saving differ from their recordings only in the record of the declaration, whose denoted objects are two, and the two Cagetti–De Nardi encodings by the family list; those recordings, which already differ from the package at the base, are not re-recorded.
  • The change was merged into main in pull request 17 at d1d45f559.

docs.title: 2026-10-20 — Category meanings and indexed data in the language guide
docs.text: • Stages now gives separate examples for parameter-defined integer indices and integer states with recorded category meanings. The reference explains calibration order, numerical keys and admitted index domains; Periods explains category-preserving connections and collection order. The guide distinguishes category domains from the forms currently admitted as collection index sets.

docs.title: 2026-10-20 — Named integer domains with category codes
docs.text:
• A set may be defined by name as a comprehension after :=, HouseholdStatus := {i : ℤ | i >= 0, i <= 1}, a form refused under syntax before; a field declared on the name has the set as its domain, and to_source writes the assignment back in that spelling (syntax/grammars/stage.lark, rule assigned_value; syntax/lower.py; syntax/source.py; Symbols and conventions). AAS requested such named domains on 19 October 2026, with the meanings of their members given by an annotation, for a field whose values are categories.
  • The marker !categories, alone or followed by one identifier, gives each member of such a set one category: HouseholdStatus := {i : ℤ | i >= 0, i <= 1} :: [!categories household_status, newborn=0, old=1] is the set {0, 1} with the category map 0 ↦ newborn, 1 ↦ old. Every other entry but an id= entry and a double-quoted description is name=code, a stage identifier and an integer, so that 0, -0 and 00 are one code. The set is a comprehension over ℤ or ℕ whose conditions compare its one binder with integer literals by inequalities; both bounds are required, the range is not empty, under ℕ the lower bound is at least 1, and each member has one category. The new module typing/category_codes.py makes these checks where the fold builds the set's record; the marker's spelling and the checks are decisions of the brief named-integer-domains-and-category-meanings.md, not rulings of AAS.
  • Elaboration refuses under the rule category-codes, at the set's file position and naming every failed check, a marked set that fails one, as the entry old=2 does by giving a code outside the set and leaving the member 1 without a category; the marker written as a key, twice or without codes; a bare or single-quoted tag; a code given to two categories, old=-0 beside newborn=0 among them; and a marked set that is ℤ, an interval, {0, …, 1}, {0, 1}, a set of names, a restriction of a coded set, a range bounded by a parameter, or a range with an equality condition, i = 1, which a comprehension may hold since the entry below. It also refuses the marker on any item but a top-level named set, at that item, and a field declared on a coded set at one site and on another set at another (Refusals). Double-quoted entries, ["!categories household_status"], and a tag that only begins with the marker, [!categories_status], mark nothing.
  • The set's record keeps the map as Definition.categories, a frozen records.CategoryCodes of the identifier, or None, and the (code, name) pairs in increasing code order (native/records.py; fold/stage_fold.py). The marked set's definition denotes the set and the map, the second a Denoted whose expression is the record; the supporting definitions that denote() answers for the stage and for a builder hold both, and the set's card prints the map on the row under the set, 0 ↦ newborn, 1 ↦ old (categories household_status) (stage/denotations.py; display/cards.py; The definitions table).
  • The stage's encoding writes categories, the identifier and the pairs, on the stored entry of a marked set and on no other entry, and an encoded answer writes the map as a node records.CategoryCodes; the schema stage-encoding/2.6 is extended in place with both, as it was for unread_inputs on 17 October 2026 (stage/encoding.py; display/answer_encoding.py; display/encoding_checks.py; display/stage-encoding-2.6.schema.json).
  • Two connected fields on coded domains are compatible exactly when each code the writing domain may hold is a member of the reading domain and stands there for the same category, factor by factor for a product. A coded domain and an uncoded one are incompatible, a restriction of a coded set is compatible into the set but the set is not compatible into the restriction, and a restriction keeps the codes within the bounds its literal conditions, inequalities or equalities such as j = 1, place on its binder. Where another condition leaves its members undetermined, the pair is not established where the answer depends on them, as it is for a pair out of a restriction by a parameter into a set whose codes disagree, since the restriction may hold no member; the same restriction by a parameter on both sides of a pair within one period is one set, but not one whose condition calls a function, whose value the names alone do not fix. The category named c is (κ, c), κ the identifier or, without one, the stage text's SHA-256 digest with the set's name, so that one text joined to its occurrence in the next period is compatible and two texts with equal maps and no identifier are not; a stage made by make_stage from a syntax tree holds no digest, and the pairs of its local categories are not established. _Types.checked of factory/connections.py decides authored, inferred and inter-period pairs alike from the codes, read before any name is resolved, and the reason given for an incompatible pair names both maps (Period syntax).
  • A connector converts no code. A stage whose authored transition writes one set's codes as another's recodes them: with Recoded := {i : ℤ | i >= 0, i <= 1} :: [!categories household_status, newborn=1, old=0] and n_next : Recoded, the line n_next = 1 - n recodes the status, and the pairs into and out of that stage are compatible, whereas the direct pair into the opposite codes is not. The package does not check that such a transition preserves the categories.
  • A named comprehension without the marker defines its set alone, with no category map, and two fields on such domains are compared as uncoded domains are, by the comparison of sets, which reads the binder as a parameter, so that the pair is not established; where the stages declare a parameter of the binder's name, that parameter is read in the binder's place, and a pair within one period is then compatible while a pair between periods is not established. A bare category constant is still refused: n_next = old is refused under name-in-scope, whether old names a category of a coded set or a label of Nb := {newborn, old}.
  • validate_encoding refuses a stored categories on an entry that is no set, and a map, stored or in an answer, whose codes do not increase strictly or whose names repeat, the checks records.CategoryCodes makes (display/encoding_checks.py). Bellman Workbench lists a marked set once among the definitions a box uses, since the set denotes two objects under one identity (bellman_workbench/model.py, _definitions_named); before this, the Details panel of every box that read such a set failed to render.
  • The parsed terms of the 48 stage files under applications/ are unchanged, and the encodings of the 42 that elaborate differ from their encodings before this change only in the digest of stage.lark under provenance.versions.grammar; their printed cards are unchanged. The tests are packages/bellman/tests/test_category_codes.py, with one test for each of the brief's acceptance items 1 to 6, 37 cases in all, the sixth checking the executed notebook of the verification folder 2026-10-20-category-codes; the example of category-codes in refusal_examples.py; and a test of the Workbench's rows in packages/bellman-workbench/tests/test_model.py.
  • The change was merged into main in pull request 16 at aee75f198.

docs.title: 2026-10-20 — Products and equality conditions in feasible sets
docs.text:
• A feasibility correspondence may have a product body, Γ(z : ℝ₊) := [0, z] × ℝ₊, preserving factor order and dependence on the argument (Constraints §1).
  • A set comprehension may contain equality alongside inequalities, Γ(z : ℝ₊) := {q : ℝ₊ × ℝ₊ × ℝ₊ | q[1] + q[2] = z}. Its member is one product-valued quantity, and the policy retains the complete coupled feasible set for its joint choice (Equation parsing rules §2).
  • Source writing, definitions, policy denotations and structured exports preserve product coordinates and the complete relation. Applying the correspondence replaces its formal arguments throughout the set, with the comprehension's member remaining bound.

docs.title: 2026-10-19 — Finite index sets and the collections declared on them
docs.text:
• A stage file may define a finite set of integers whose bounds name parameters, L_J := {1, …, J}, and a listed finite set of integer keys whose members name parameters, S_θ := {0, θ} ⊂ ℤ; a bare {a, b} still lists two labels. Integer literals are retained without a floating-point conversion (Symbols and conventions).
  • A parameter, a field or a shock may be declared on the functions from such a set, δ : L_J → ℝ, dist : L_J × L_J → ℝ₊, ε : I_J → ℝ; δ[j] selects the entry at a key declared on the index set, and dist[j][i] the entry at the ordered pair, the first key on the first factor. A parameter the index set reads is among the arguments of every kernel that selects on it, so one kernel compiled before binding serves every calibration.
  • calibrate takes such a collection as a sequence in the members' order, nested for a product, or as a mapping keyed by the members' integers or labels; it refuses a wrong count, a missing or surplus key and an entry outside the entries' set, naming the declaration and the key or pair, and a value for a fixed product is checked entry by entry (Binding verbs §2). Entries may be real-valued. A Categorical whose rows are named parameters, (Q_h, Q_m, Q_l)[e_c] or Π[e_c], has each row checked at the values, one entry per member, in the unit interval and summing to one; a written weight vector has one weight per member.
  • The obligations index-set-bounds and index-set-members retain, until calibration, that a range's bounds are integers in order and that listed members are distinct integers in their declared set. AAS restricted numerical indexing to integer keys; noninteger members, bounds and supplied keys are refused without rounding or truncation. Integral floating values identify their exact integer, and distinct large integers remain distinct through calibration, connections and compiled selection.
  • A selection by a position that is no whole number, x[2.5], which was read as the second position, is refused (Equation parsing rules).
  • A set of functions on a set that is no finite index set, δ : ℝ → ℝ, a range or a listed set whose written numbers already break its conditions, {1, …, 2.5}, {0, 2.5} ⊂ ℝ or {0, 0.0} ⊂ ℤ, and a selection by a key declared on no finite set are refused at construction; a member or a bound that a calibration makes a boolean, infinite or undefined, and two mapping keys identifying the same integer, refuse the calibration.
  • Two connected fields on finite label sets are compatible when the writing set's labels lie in the reading set, and fields valued in collections only when their index sets list the same members in the same order.
  • Compiled numerical selection uses machine integers and refuses unsupported parameter-dependent division in index expressions, with a separately declared integer parameter as the alternative. Symbols and conventions states the compilation rules.

docs.title: 2026-10-18 — The documentation homepage: photographs of the decisions the language models
docs.text:
• The hero holds both of the brand's loops, the arrival loop at the left and the decision loop at the right.
  • The properties stand on a looping overhead video of a market. Over it a field of the brand's modules, drawn as wire frames, starts scattered, settles into a floating grid, packs into bullets and recedes to the horizon as the reader scrolls.
  • Six photographs follow, each held on screen while its own field of modules does the same: the Sydney Harbour Bridge half built (stages joined into one model), a railroad roundhouse (work and retirement), a street of houses (housing), a vegetable seller's boat on Dal Lake (consumption and saving), Sydney Harbour from the air (heterogeneous agents) and a bank's hall (interest rates). Each names the decision its model solves and links to the model; each caption credits the photograph. The page carries no script.

docs.title: 2026-10-17 — Bellman Workbench: the page made clean (design pass 13)
docs.text:
• After five independent reviews of the page and an adversarial check of their synthesis, the graph and the chrome share one system. In both graphs every port is one 6-px square in one ink, a plug filled and a socket hollow, centered on the edge and on its wire; a cable, a stub and a wire are 1.3 px in one color, and a stroke never draws thinner than a pixel on the screen; the bus mark is a slash in the port ink with its count above the cable, or below it for the lower cable of a stage with two plugs; a marker stands 24 px outside the period's frame, an outside marker drawing the far stage's port (§8).
  • A stage's card is 32 px, its name, chevron, socket and plug on one axis, its builders a 3-px strip under the name in the tints of their signatures, every card of a column of one width; the chevron opens the occurrence with its builders, and the selected card unfolds to a band naming each builder; the period frame has a 24-px head and one top edge with its neighbors, and the drawing stands at the region's top in the opening and fitted views (§7).
  • The chrome returns to the five type styles and the grid of its design system: Code name for a stage's key wherever it heads a row, card or selection, the path in the interface face, the Recipe's heads in Small and its rows in 16-px lines with the trash at the row's end, Details' keys in sentence case, the editor's line numbers on the text's baseline, no outer margin at the window's right edge, and one mark for each state: an accent edge for an active control or tab, the selection wash with a 3-px bar for a selected row, the hover wash alone for hover; the problems count in the refusal's orange; destructive acts as text buttons after Details' rows (§§2, 4, 7).
  • On 18 October a second round of the five reviews read the built page, and a fix wave answered its findings. In both graphs each stage keeps one row, in the order of the recipe's list, in every period, and no two cables share a run or cross. A plug from which a cable leaves is filled. Edges and marks keep at least one pixel on the screen at every zoom and take no width from the layout. A hovered or selected cable draws no label: its branch stands first in its hover text and in Details, and a selected cable rings its two movable ports. Stubs bend outside the period's frame, closed periods share the frames' top edge, and + Stage and + Period are drawn at the view's scale. Selecting a card pans the view when the unfolded card would leave it, and the opening view begins at the column's text edge.
  • In the chrome, the Recipe's rows are 48 px, so four stand whole at the panel's default height. The graph bar keeps one row: in a narrow column its visible name is withdrawn and remains the region's heading for screen readers. Details' blocks stand 8 px apart, with the removal buttons last. The bars and the perch tables stand on whole pixels. Details' heads print the identifier in Code name and the kind of piece in Small, the labels are in sentence case, and a stage's path reads durables › spec.yml › tenure › periods[0]. Lists, menus and the editor's lint tooltip share one form for hover, selection and overlays.
  • The chrome and the fix wave were merged into main on 21 October 2026 from codex/model-interface-q, after the continuous-distribution work of 19 to 21 October had been merged into the branch; the graph had been merged on 17 October at 687b123fd.

docs.title: 2026-10-17 — The comparator reads two spellings the elaborator reads alike as one
docs.text: • _normalised of packages/meaning-map-training/meaning_map_training/compare.py writes a single tuple argument of max or min as the argument list, max((x, 0)) as max(x, 0), and restricts a backward block's inputs to those its lines read, the bodies of called definitions included, removing the wire of an input left out from the block's builder; a forward block's listing is kept, since it fixes the perch at which a shock is drawn. Bloom and Deaton of EPOCH-005 pass-v0 and Gourinchas–Parker of EPOCH-006 pass-v1, re-compared from their saved declarations, come out equal where they were recorded undecided; the records stay as written. Three tests on the toy stage (commit 4d9c5e37a; brief AI/road-map/AI-todos/briefs-for-agents/comparator-two-small-fixes-brief.md).

docs.title: 2026-10-17 — The joint search of the trellis comparison reads the per-stage results
docs.text: • compare_trellises visits only the stage pairings whose every pair compared equal on its own and, within them, only the renamings under which those pairs compare equal (_stage_name_maps, from the renaming search with every group of names the colours cannot tell apart permuted, each verified once), and checks the inter-period joins on each; a pair that compared undecided leaves the verdict undecided, candidates_tried counts the renamings verified and the joint candidates checked, so its values are not comparable with earlier profiles, and DEFAULT_BOUND and the profile's fields are unchanged. FUES of EPOCH-005 pass-v0, whose six stage pairs were equal and whose search exhausted the bound on the wrong pairing of its two consumption stages, comes out equal in 12 candidates under either keying of the right-hand files; a trellis whose only pairing holds an unequal pair is now different, not undecided. Two tests (commit 2e7586c17).

docs.title: 2026-10-17 — Bellman Workbench: a backward header that lists an input no line reads is a problem to review
docs.text:
• The list under the error mark holds one line for each value input a backward header of the stage shown lists and no line of its block reads, the package's diagnostic unread-input (stage.diagnostics()["unread_inputs"]; AAS, 17 October 2026): the package's sentence, "the header lists dV[>], which no line of the block reads", with the file and the line of the block's header, counted among the problems to review and not among the errors, under the heading Headers to check, a group of its own beside Connections to check. The stage is elaborated and drawn as before, since the package refuses nothing. A line of the list carries the rule the package names (Refusal.rule), a connection's rule for a connection to check and unread-input for a header (app.py, standing_refusals, ErrorMark, UNREAD_INPUT_RULE).
  • The portfolio model's cons.bl lists dV[>] on its policy header and its one line reads V[>] alone, so the model shows one such line at declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl:29. Tests: tests/test_unread_input.py, the brief's acceptance item 4; three tests of test_app.py and test_model.py on that model expect the line, and the backward graph's inputs 𝑉≻ alone. test_model.py's comparison of the classification table read from a text with the one read from its construction fails on cons.bl, since the text lists dV[>] at the continuation perch and the construction's fields leave it out; how the table is to show a listed field the block does not take is a decision for the Workbench and is named in the brief's report.

docs.title: 2026-10-17 — A value input a backward header lists and no line reads is left out of the builder and recorded as a diagnostic
docs.text:
• A value input a backward block's header lists and no line of the block reads is admitted, and the block's box leaves it out: the block's signature, its builder and the formal arguments of the builder's kernels are the same whether or not the header lists it, so two declarations of one model that differ by such a listing elaborate to the same block signatures and builders (AAS's ruling of 17 October 2026, following the issue on the trellis comparison; the brief elaborator-unread-listed-input-brief.md). The listing counts as the field's consumption for the check that every field of a complete stage is consumed, so a file that elaborated before still elaborates, and a decision-perch value such a listing alone consumed stands among unused_outputs. A block whose lines read no value input keeps its listed inputs as the formal input of its kernels, since the header must list one (rule value-input-role). A value input a line reads and the header omits is refused under signature-complete as before; forward headers and controls are unchanged. (typing/declarations.py, Declarations.unread_value_inputs; stage/construction.py; native/records.py, BlockData.unread_inputs and BlockHeader.unread; fold/block_lines.py, unread_inputs_of.)
  • The elaboration records each such listing as a diagnostic in the form of the connection diagnostics, now the record bellman.refusals.Diagnostic, which factory/connections.py imports: the rule unread-input, the block as its address, the input's identity as its one candidate and the sentence "the header lists dV[>], which no line of the block reads". stage.diagnostics() answers nine questions, the ninth unread_inputs, carried across versions, printed one line per diagnostic as <block>: <sentence>, and written in the encoding under diagnostics.unread_inputs as records of their five fields, which the schema stage-encoding/2.6 admits and requires; the training's items and the Matsya export copy the encoding's diagnostics and need no change. The corpus stage cons.bl carries one such diagnostic, its policy header listing dV[>] that its one line does not read, and its policy builder now reads 𝑉≻ alone.
  • The copier of the native objects (native/hypergraphs.py, copy_native) copies a named tuple as its own class, since a version made by a binding verb carries the kept diagnostics and refused the Diagnostic inside them.
