  • Every call is recorded with its step and cycle, and the message is sent as ordered parts with the instruction text and the guide pages first as the prefix marked for the provider's prompt cache. The command matsya-serve starts the service.

docs.title: 2026-10-07 — The gestures of the trellis graph
docs.text:
• In the forward trellis graph a field that no join reaches or reads shows a port; dragging from a continuation port to an arrival port types the connector into the period file or the trellis file through the editor, flat where the names are unambiguous and keyed otherwise, and the file opens at the written line. An arrival that joins already reach takes a further source, written as a further key of the mapping that holds the join; a continuation field joins once; a branching stage's ports carry the branch's label, keep: w_kp≻.
  • A join wire is selected by a click and removed by Backspace, Delete or remove in Details, or moved by dragging one of its ends; each is one edit of the text that the editor's undo reverses where the file was open. A model left with unjoined fields is drawn, not refused, the fields marked on their boxes and counted on the status line.
  • A stage is added by dropping it from the stage list on a period, or by Enter; a period is added by the + period controls, with the form add period; the trellis written as records takes the entry directly.
  • The undo history begins afresh when another file's document replaces the current one, so an undo never restores another file's text into the open tab.

docs.title: 2026-10-07 — Bellman Workbench in four columns
docs.text:
• Bellman Workbench stands in four columns on dark surfaces: the folder, the text with the BellmanType panel under it, the graph with Details under it, and Matsya. The buttons files and Matsya fold the folder and Matsya's column to narrow rails, the browser keeps the folds with the regions' sizes, and a narrowing window narrows Matsya, then the graph, then folds the folder. Every face is served from the package: Archivo, IBM Plex Mono and STIX Two Math (Bellman Workbench §1).
  • The text has one tab per file opened, each closed by its × unless its text is unsaved; the icon hide types and the button Save stand at the right of the tabs. The stage's name is drawn large, an annotation stands at the right of its statement, a wrapped line is indented by four characters, and a minimap at the editor's right edge moves the editor to the line of the mark clicked (Bellman Workbench §2).
  • The tab Fields holds its three tables side by side, headed ≺ arrival, ∼ decision and ≻ continuation, with no line column: a field's name is a button that moves the editor to its line. The panel's bar no longer names the state of the reading, and the panel keeps one height on every tab. While the construction is refused, the tables read the text's parse and stay editable, the row of a field the refusal names drawn in orange (Bellman Workbench §2).
  • The graph's header holds the choices graph (operator, initial) and direction (backward, forward) and the button trellis; a box prints its symbol alone, its ports' labels on hover; the trellis's restriction is typed in the field periods, and all shows the whole trellis again (Bellman Workbench §§2, 7).
  • Details, under the graph, holds the legend and the selected piece's rows, each on one line; with a box of the construction of the saved text selected, its button paper writes paper/<stage>.md and paper/<stage>.svg once (Bellman Workbench §3).
  • Goto Anything, opened by Command+P or Ctrl+P or the icon go to, lists blocks and boxes after @, a line after :, text after # and commands after >, shows the current result without moving the cursor, and leaves everything as it was on Escape (Bellman Workbench §3).
  • The status line is visible: the cursor's place, 8:33, the file, the occurrence, the state with the digest, constructed 08c03d3, the refusals, indent 4 and BellmanSym; more shows the details and git's line, and constructed carries on hover The language's check, not a verification of the economics. (Bellman Workbench §4).
  • Matsya fills the right column with its periwinkle Υ and answers headed MATSYA; its conversation is named by a digest of the folder's path, and BELLMAN_WORKBENCH_MATSYA=off removes the column (Bellman Workbench §5). The folder's button notebook writes notebooks/<folder>.ipynb once, whose cells assemble the trellis, print each occurrence's view, its digests and its methods (Bellman Workbench §6).
  • The hovers of the terms kind and period in Details each read as one clause: the kind of the box's operator, or block or field in an initial diagram and one date of the model, numbered from the terminal period, periods[0].

docs.title: 2026-10-06 — Matsya's model-iteration service and retrieval code
docs.text: • The optional package under packages/matsya/ gains the code that builds and searches a local index of sources, a service in which a writer, a reader and a judge iterate on a Bellman-SYM declaration within a call limit, shorter guides for each role, and records of each call that survive a failed job without holding prompts or private text. It is installed only for the development and evaluation of Matsya, and the Bellman-SYM package does not depend on it.

docs.title: 2026-10-06 — The graph drawn in the page
docs.text:
• Bellman Workbench draws its graph on navy. The header separates graph, initial diagram and trellis from backward and forward. Four icon buttons at the foot change layout direction, zoom in, zoom out and fit, with perch overlays in a stage's view. Layers open and close with ▸ and ▾. The wheel zooms and dragging the background pans (Bellman Workbench §2).
  • Tab and Shift+Tab reach the graph's boxes and bring them into view, Enter selects, and Escape clears the linked selection. Choosing a field in the Fields tab selects its box when the initial diagram containing it is shown, and selecting that box marks its row.
  • A graph that could not be laid out, or a graph file that did not load, puts its refusal in the error mark's list. export view also exports the trellis shown, with its restriction and input record.
  • The built Workbench package includes its graph files, fonts and interface files, so the installed page can draw with the network off once its dependencies are installed.
  • The Workbench no longer embeds Model Explorer's component. The lessons' view in Model Explorer is unchanged.
  • The Workbench's installation requires filelock below release 3.30, the releases from which the library slows the package's copy of a trellis in Solara's server; requirements.txt holds it at 3.29.7.
  • A later start of the Workbench on unchanged files reads the bound trellis from $XDG_CACHE_HOME/bellman-workbench/bindings/, or ~/.cache/bellman-workbench/bindings/, beside the stage views, in place of binding it again; a change of any file the trellis reads, or of the code of the package or of the Workbench, binds it again, and the folder can be removed at any time (Bellman Workbench §7).

docs.title: 2026-10-05 — The time to bind and copy a trellis
docs.text: • Binding and copying a trellis take less time, and no result changes: the package's copy of a stage version finds what it needs of each class once, a version a binding makes from another holds that version's records without freezing them again, and the occurrences of one stage text bound under different mappings compute the answers their graphs determine once. On the durables trellis of 154 stage occurrences, on one machine, specify_trellis takes 2.7 s where it took 6.1 s, one parameter draw by calibrate_trellis 1.1 s where it took 2.0 s, and the Workbench's bind_trellis, in a process without Solara, 2.0 s where it took 3.7 s.

docs.title: 2026-10-05 — Bellman Workbench, into a stage and back, and the BellmanType panel
docs.text:
• The text pane of Bellman Workbench is named BellmanSym, after the language, in place of Symbolic Bellman; the graph pane Semantic graph, in place of Denotational Semantic Graph; and the panel under the text, the classification table, the BellmanType panel, whose bar holds the state of the last reading and the tabs Fields, Parameters, Settings and Methods (AAS, 3 October 2026; Bellman Workbench §§1 and 2). The buttons that add an entry, add field, new variant, add stage and add period, show the sign + with their word on hover, and new trellis keeps its word. Every region takes its size from a handle on its edge, within a least size: the tree, the two panes, the BellmanType panel, the panel under the graph and the Matsya window; the browser keeps the sizes for the model folder, and a double click on a handle returns its region to its default size.
  • A double click on an occurrence of the trellis view, or the button open the stage of its panel, which replaces open, opens its stage file bound as the page's recipe binds it at that position, the head under the tree reading periods[3] / tenure and the status line's version bound; a double click on a box inside an occurrence opens the file at the box's block. The breadcrumb, a new first row of the window, names the path the page took, durables › spec.yml › periods[3] › tenure, and its folder, recipe and period are links. Alt+← and Alt+→, pressed outside a text field, and the buttons ← and → at the breadcrumb's start, step back and forward through the places the page has shown, each place its view, recipe, restriction, occurrence and open file with the selection there; the places are kept until the page is closed, and none is written in the model folder (Bellman Workbench §7).
  • A stage file opened from the tree is bound as its first occurrence in the page's recipe, under the breadcrumb durables › spec.yml › tenure (in 51 periods); the head offers the file's other positions, or, where the page's recipe holds none, names after held by each recipe of the folder that holds it, a link that binds the file there, under the breadcrumb durables › tenure.bl. With nothing selected, the panel lists under used at the file's positions in each recipe that holds it, the page's recipe first, each a link into that recipe's trellis, which shows the occurrence's period alone, periods 3, where the restriction in the input leaves the occurrence out.
  • The tab Fields is the classification table of 2 October. In a branching stage its continuation table heads each branch's group by the control that selects the branch and its label, cntn · d = keep, or by the label alone where nature draws the branch, and adds in every branching stage the group cntn · all branches with its own +, which writes a state into the block of every branch; the language refuses a field that two branches write, so the elaborator refuses such a state and proposes a new name for one of its copies. Parameters lists the parameters the stage declares with their values at the occurrence, or unvalued; Settings lists the settings with their kinds and values; Methods lists each target's method, with a choice among the methods the method table admits there. A typed value or a chosen method is written to the file that writes it, and a parameter that no file values is added to the last calibration file the recipe lists, which the tab names; each row links its file and line, and where the recipe lists no file of a kind, or no recipe binds the stage, the tab says so, the recipe lists no settings source for disc or no recipe values them.
  • Every refusal of the page stands in one place, except a form's, which stays in its form (git's refusal of a commit stands in both), and the Methods tab's sentence on the places of a stage and its refusal at a target, which stay in the tab: an error mark at the right end of the window's first row shows in orange the count of what stands refused or undone, and a click opens the list under it, newest first, each line the refusal's sentence, as the package, the Workbench or git writes it, with nothing added, followed, where the refusal names them, by its file and line, a link that opens the file at that line, or by its file alone; with nothing refused the mark is drawn in slate and the list reads nothing refused. The list holds the refusals of the open text and of the trellis, the bindings skipped or refused, a refused change of Fields, a refused value, method or choice of a file, a refused restriction, git's refusal of a commit or a push, a refused export, and a save that met a changed file. What was refused keeps a mark in orange in its own place and no longer prints the sentence there: the panel's line, refused at … or refused in …, with the rule, the cell of Fields or the input or choice of another tab that was refused, the button replace of the recipe table's entry, the restriction's input, the button of git's line whose command was refused, and the frame of a save's three choices (AAS, 4 October 2026; Bellman Workbench §3).
  • The page's words are shorter (AAS, 4 October 2026): a label is a word or a few, Select a box., Select an occurrence., No stage file., Not elaborated.; a hover carries at most one short sentence; a form's note says in one line what it writes and where; a refusal of the package is its sentence with nothing added, and a refusal of the Workbench's own names in one line what is wrong and where, the recipe lists no settings source for disc where the tab added ; add one in the recipe table, or declaration/spec.yml holds unsaved text. On 4 October 2026, in a change made apart from this work on the repository's main branch, a box of the graph came to show its symbol alone, 𝑉≻ ∘ 𝑔≻, its kind standing among its rows in the panel, and the legend to name its marks in a few words, bound method, at a policy and law of motion (Bellman Workbench §2).
  • The package's replace_entry of bellman.trellis writes a number, a boolean and a tag as well as a string, plain as YAML writes them, 1.05, 400, true and !pchip, where before it wrote strings alone, giving β: "0.95" for the number 0.95; and entry_value refuses with a ValueError a text holding a value that the package's reader of YAML files cannot build, such as !!bool abc, and a text nested deeper than the reader follows, where the reader's own error escaped before, a KeyError, an IndexError, an AttributeError, a TypeError, an OverflowError or a RecursionError (The trellis factory §8).

docs.title: 2026-10-04 — Model translation tools
docs.text:
• Added programs for comparing declared models, constructing controlled changes, recording translations between model descriptions and declarations, and summarising their results. The first recorded run uses scripted responses; the first measurement with language models remains to be made.
  • Registered 38 models for the first automated iteration study: ten Econometrica papers, fourteen HARK models and fourteen applications. An input report lists available preparation files, unresolved source relationships and descriptions or declarations still to generate; registration grants no verification grade.
  • Every model in the additional application corpus follows the same model directory layout as applications/, with model notes named economics.md and one folder per declared stage. Each Econometrica model folder contains its reference paper, model note and declaration folder.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 — The trellis view in seconds
docs.text:
• The package's new operation specify_trellis(syntactic, previous=None, kinds=KINDS) of bellman.trellis answers the specified trellis of a syntactic trellis, equal to the trellis that elaborate_trellis and the trellis verbs of kinds make, the verbs applied in the order calibrate, methodize, configure: each distinct stage text is constructed once, or taken from previous, and each stage occurrence is copied once, where the elaboration and each verb copy every occurrence. assemble_trellis(directory, recipe) is specify_trellis(load_recipe(directory, recipe)) (The Bellman factory §2), and a refused binding carries the note Binding kind: <kind> beside the note that names the occurrence. The durables trellis, of 154 occurrences, is bound with 154 copies of a stage where the elaboration and two verbs made 462.
  • Bellman Workbench reads a trellis through specify_trellis, with the trellis shown before as its previous; a kind of binding the package refuses is reported and left out of the next call, so that the other kinds still bind. A reading in which no file the trellis reads has changed on disk is not repeated: a new restriction draws the trellis held, in under 0.1 s on durables, where the trellis was read again in about 7 s, and the page reads a folder's trellis once when it opens the folder, where it made two identical readings at the same time.
  • A trellis of more than six periods opens on its terminal period and the two before it, the window writing periods 0–2 into the input above the graph as a reader would, and the status line names the number of periods of the whole trellis after a restriction of periods alone, shown periods 0–2 of 51 (10 occurrences); a trellis of six periods or fewer shown after a long one opens whole (Bellman Workbench §7).
  • The view of each stage of a trellis is kept between runs as one JSON file for each stage version, a stage text with its three bindings, and each of its two graphs, backward and forward, in $XDG_CACHE_HOME/bellman-workbench/views/, or ~/.cache/bellman-workbench/views/ where the variable is not set. The folder of the views is named by the package's version and a digest of its source files, of Python's major and minor version and of the installed versions of the package's pinned dependencies and of Model Explorer, as a process finds them when it imports bellman.factory.model_explorer, so that a change of the package's files or of those versions gives another folder; the version of no other distribution is part of the name. Among the cases in which the name does not describe the code that computes a view are these two: a process that loaded some of the package's modules before its files changed, and imports bellman.factory.model_explorer after the change, computes views with its older code in the folder named for the new files; and a process that imports that module before an upgrade of Model Explorer, and exports for the first time after the upgrade, computes views with the newer Model Explorer, and reads those of the older one, in the folder named for the older version. The folder can be removed at any time (Bellman Workbench §7). The tests of both packages set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a temporary folder.
  • Measured on the durables folder under periods 0–2 on one machine: the Workbench's first reading of the trellis in a fresh process takes 5.17 to 5.37 s with no stage view kept and 3.37 to 3.46 s with the views kept, where it took 7.1 to 7.3 s before this work; opened in the page by a new server, the trellis was drawn after 6.7 s the first time and after 4.9 and 5.0 s the second, in two runs.

docs.title: 2026-10-03 — The legend, the text on a box and the colors of the graph
docs.text:
• The box of a primitive operator, in the view in Model Explorer and in Bellman Workbench's graph pane, reads two short lines: the kind of its operator, followed by at and the policies where the operator is stated at a policy, above the symbol the drawing shows for it without the arguments of a law or an aggregator written out at a policy, Pullback at 𝑐 above 𝑉≻ ∘ 𝑔≻. A law of motion is named as the operator's card names it, so that the pullback and the push-forward that read one law name it alike, 𝑉≻ ∘ 𝑔≻ and 𝑔≻∗μ, where the drawing writes the letter 𝑔; a method bound within the box ends the second line, 𝑉(m_d), 𝑑𝑉(m_d) · !Cartesian; the arguments stand in the operator's rule rows; and Inputs, Outputs and the nodes of an initial diagram keep one line (node_label in packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py; The view in Model Explorer §3.1). AAS found the text on a box "too big and uninformative" on 2 October 2026.
  • An evaluation is labeled by the outputs it produces, 𝑉(m_d), 𝑑𝑉(m_d), in place of the words at the output, in the drawing that diagram() answers as in the view; an evaluation with three or more outputs names the first two and counts the others, 𝑉(a_d, h_d, z_d), 𝑑𝑉_a(a_d, h_d, z_d) and 1 more, and its tooltip in the drawing, its card and its output ports name them all (box_symbol in packages/bellman/bellman/display/drawing.py). Lessons 01 and 02 say so, the lesson kernels names the aggregation of cntn_to_dcsn by its two lines, Aggregation at 𝑐 over 𝐺, and the thirteen lessons are recorded again.
  • The view is written as two files, the graph file and the file of the three perch overlays, and serve(graph_path, …) takes the graph file alone: the method overlay, which tinted each operator within which a method is bound by the operation the method realizes, is retired with its node data file and with method_overlay, and a bound method is the one mark at the end of its box's label (The view in Model Explorer §1, §2 and §4.2). Seven lessons count the view's two files.
  • The colors of the view tell apart the levels a reader opens and what each builder gives (AAS, 3 October 2026: "these need to be only three or four colors"): a node is white with a navy border and a navy label; the node of an operator that writes a wire read outside its builder's layer, by another builder, by Outputs or by a join of a trellis, is lined in ultramarine; a layer is lined in navy, a period of a trellis white, a stage occurrence on the lightest of the site's three pale blues, a builder on the second and a sub-builder on the third, and the perch layers of an initial diagram on the lightest; and the node of a refused graph keeps its orange line. The fills by operator family and the slate of Inputs and Outputs are gone, and bellman.stage and bellman.trellis export LAYER_COLORS, NODE_STYLE, OUTPUT_STYLE and PERCH_COLORS in place of FAMILY_STYLES and METHOD_TINTS (The view in Model Explorer §3.1; The API §2).
  • The legend under Bellman Workbench's graph lists what the graph shown holds and nothing else: as its title the label of the version drawn, cons methodized; the levels the graph draws, each with a swatch of its fill and border; each bound method's tag and place, !egm policy:Evaluation, a place in a trellis written with its stage's key and without its period, !Cartesian cons/cntn_to_dcsn:Evaluation, and listed once; the marks the labels hold, · !tag, at 𝑐 and 𝑔≺, 𝑔≻, each with a sentence that says what it means; the color of each perch while perch overlays is on; and in a field diagram each role with its fields, value V≻, V, V≺. The swatches of the operator families and the catalogue of method tags are gone, the catalogue standing on Method types. The Workbench draws a selected box, the boxes it reads from and writes to, and the wires between them in ultramarine, where the viewer's own colors are green and orange (legend_entries and Legend in packages/bellman-workbench/bellman_workbench/app.py, and brand.css; Bellman Workbench §2).

docs.title: 2026-10-03 — A trellis view drawn once per stage version
docs.text: • The view of a trellis in Model Explorer computes one stage view and one builders hypergraph per stage version, the text and the three bindings of an occurrence, and gives it to every occurrence of that version, in place of one computation per occurrence; the drawn view is the same, node for node. The fifty-one periods of the durables model, 154 occurrences of four versions, are exported in 5 seconds where they took 82, and the Workbench's trellis view opens in seconds (AAS, 3 October 2026: the twenty-second load of the durables folder).

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — Bellman Workbench, the trellis and the recipe
docs.text:
• Bellman Workbench (packages/bellman-workbench/, the page Bellman Workbench §7) shows the trellis a model folder elaborates to: a folder with a recipe or with trellis files opens on its trellis, each period a frame holding its stage occurrences and each occurrence its builders, the button trellis returning to it from a stage. The trellis is read again whenever a file it reads is saved, a changed stage file constructed once and every occurrence of it replaced. Typing periods 0–2, stages cons, port or both shows part of the trellis, a join that leaves it standing at the view's own inputs or outputs with the occurrence outside named. A refused backward graph lists each join that leaves a marginal value unpaired with a link to the header that declares the wire and to the connector.
  • The recipe stands as a table under the tree at the head's occurrence, and where a folder's declaration/ holds several recipes, spec.yml and its variants spec.<name>.yml, they are listed above the table; a cell takes a methods, calibration or settings file of the matching folder of declaration/, or for a methods cell a stage folder's methods.yml, written in place of one entry of the recipe, by its path from the recipe's folder, with its comments and layout kept, and the stage's view and the trellis show what it binds. The open stage file is bound as the occurrence the head names where that is one of its occurrences. A slot left to fill stands in orange in the table; the slots answers.yml marks required, or every slot where it holds no list of slots, are entries of the checklist above the tree, which counts them apart from the refusals (Bellman Workbench §6). With the cursor on a name, the panel lists its occurrences, its declaration first, its calibration line and the boxes that depend on it: a box whose kernel reads or writes the name, a box one of whose wires carries it, and a box whose record rests on one of the name's definitions, directly or through the definitions those use.
  • The package gives the view of part of a trellis, to_model_explorer(trellis, periods=…, stages=…), and unpaired_joins, the rows of a refused backward graph as records (The view in Model Explorer §5); and, in bellman.trellis, entry_span, entry_value, replace_entry, append_to_mapping, append_to_sequence and written_at, which find, read, replace and append one entry of a model's YAML files as text, a quoted value keeping its quotes, and move an address of the expanded trellis to the file that writes it, counting a period file's own repeat and refusing an inter_connectors[h] that no file writes (The trellis factory §8). bellman.stage now exports PERCH_MARK, the mark a printed name carries after its letters for each perch, as in V≻ at the continuation and μ≺ at the arrival, with none at the decision, by which the Workbench matches a field in a kernel with or without its mark.
  • After the merge with the model folder's layout (the entry below), Bellman Workbench reads a folder's recipes in its declaration/, declaration/spec.yml first and its variants after it in name order, and a folder whose declaration/ holds no recipe offers its trellis files, as the eight declaration/trellis.*.yml of applications/cons-port/. A recipe at the folder's top is not read: a folder that holds spec.yml there and no recipe in declaration/ offers no source, not even its trellis files, and the panel of the open stage file says that the Workbench reads a folder's recipe at declaration/spec.yml, the sentence of the layout's apply_bindings, a function this work had deleted (model_sources and find_occurrence in bellman_workbench/recipe.py). The merge keeps bellman_workbench/yaml_text.py deleted: new variant reads the files it copies with entry_value and writes the lines that name the copies with replace_entry of bellman.trellis, a quoted value keeping its quotes, and then opens the variant's recipe as a click on it in the tree does, its trellis in the view and the variant beside the first recipe in the list. The layout's replace_scalar and replace_entry write the same text for every replacement new variant makes in the six recipes of applications/. Where replace_scalar refused, replace_entry writes a plain value that would read as another type, 2026, in double quotes, writes a double-quoted value with an escape anew within its quotes, and replaces whole a plain value written over two lines, a mapping and a tagged value, whose tag it drops; both refuse an anchored value that an alias reads and an entry the file does not hold, each with its own sentence. The claims of the layout's test of replace_scalar stand in the package's test of replace_entry (packages/bellman/tests/test_behaviour.py). The package's append_to_mapping, which add stage calls, appends after a text written with | as the last entry of a mapping, which the appender of yaml_text refused, and refuses a text written with |+ there, whose kept blank line the new entry would cut.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — The model folder's layout
docs.text:
• Every model folder under applications/ takes one layout (AAS, 2 October 2026: "proceed with the above restructure"). The files the language reads stand in the folder's declaration/: the recipe spec.yml and its variants spec.<name>.yml, the trellis and period files beside them, calibration/, settings/, and one folder per stage, stages/<key>/, holding the stage file <key>.bl, its methods file methods.yml and its note <key>.md. Beside declaration/ stand README.md, economics.md (the former model.md), code/ for the folder's programs, tests/ for its structural tests, reference/ for the papers it keeps, and results/, which git ignores (applications/.gitignore). The 206 files moved are, by folder: benhabib-2019 20, buffer-stock 1, cagetti-denardi-2006 36, cons-port 39, consumption-savings-iid 3, durables 22, epstein-zin-savings 4, housing-frictions 9, housing-owner 7, housing-renting 21, pension-retirement 8, portfolio-choice 14, retirement-choice 17 and smooth-ambiguity-savings 5. The folder cons-port/, which has no recipe, holds its eight trellis files of records in declaration/ as trellis.<name>.yml and trellis.reference-<name>.yml, and the earlier YAML stages of syntax/ in reference/legacy/syntax/. Each of the thirteen other folders gains a README.md that states the model in one sentence and the command bellman-workbench applications/<model> that opens it.
  • The documentation states the layout once, on the page Model directory layout, which is rewritten. It holds the tree of the durables folder and the parts other folders hold, the six rules of the layout, the three kinds of variant (of the route, of the values and of an equation) and the rule for the paths of a model's documents, which write a path from the model folder and keep a path quoted from a recipe or a trellis file as that file writes it. The six rules are that every file the language reads stands under declaration/, the registry load_recipe is given; that a recipe and a trellis file write every path they read; that the files of a stage stand in one folder; that variants stand side by side; that README.md is a folder's first page and economics.md its economics; and that the recordings of a model's stage files stand with the package's tests and the model's code writes into results/, which git ignores; a model folder tracks a generated file only as a record kept on purpose, such as cons-port's fixed numerical reference. applications/README.md lists the layout and names the page; Workflow, Bellman Workbench §1, The Bellman factory §3, Recipe functions §§1 and 2.1, The trellis factory §1, The runner §§2 and 4, the wiki entry Specification factory, the example pages Buffer Stock Consumption Model (Normalized), Consumption-Savings with IID Shocks, Housing Model and Port-with-Shocks Model, and §§2.1, 3.3 and 4 of the model interface specification 0.3 follow the layout or point to the page. The documents of the model folders, the docstring of applications/durables/code/wage_schedule.py and the branching corpus's page on the Cagetti and De Nardi model write their paths by the page's rule, and the cons-port lesson 03 names its methods files by their paths from the repository root in every cell.
  • Each application's recipe, six recipes in five folders, writes stage: stages/<key>/<key>.bl and names a stage's methods file stages/<key>/methods, and each trellis file of records writes its paths from its new folder; the two recipes of the package's test corpus, which are not model folders, keep stage: stages/<key>.bl. The eight recipes of the applications and of the test corpus answer the syntactic trellises they answered before, record for record, apart from the moved paths and the comments that name them: the new test packages/bellman/tests/test_layout.py compares each with the digests of packages/bellman/tests/fixtures/layout_base_trellises.json, refuses a model folder that departs from the layout, and checks that a recipe whose stage: names the earlier path is refused as load_stage refuses a missing file. Every reader of a moved path is repointed in the same change, except the notebooks outside tutorials/, which this unit does not edit, among them cons-port's frozen legacy notebook applications/cons-port/notebooks/port-cons/solve_port_cons_ffp.ipynb, which still reads ../../syntax and so no longer runs where it stands. The readers repointed are the application tests; the package's tests and fixtures, the corpus test collecting */declaration/stages/*/*.bl; the 44 recordings that store a stage file's path, written again, which differ from the earlier ones in the paths alone and in where a printed line holding a longer path breaks; Bellman Workbench, which reads a folder's recipe from declaration/spec.yml and takes a stage folder's methods.yml for a methods file (bellman_workbench/model.py, _recipe and _role); the decision records and the project's rules and guides; the root README.md; the pages of the documentation; and the cells of the thirteen lessons and their set-up module tutorials/checkout.py.
  • The thirteen lessons of tutorials/ are executed again once, by tutorials/tools/execute_lessons.py --record, after their cells were repointed, and tutorials/lessons.json records their new digests and the paths of their inputs that moved, 82 entries for 46 files; --check finds all thirteen up to date. Eight recorded outputs change, each because it prints a moved path or a file whose comment names one: the stage occurrence that lesson 01 of the getting-started series prints and two that the Benhabib lesson prints, which now break the longer path over two lines; the comment of the calibration file calibration/portfolio.yml that lesson 04 prints; the trellis file trellis.port-cons.yml that lesson 05 and cons-port lesson 02 print; and the recipe and the provenance of the sources that the Benhabib lesson prints. No other output and no cell's source changes.
  • A stage card's File section breaks a path wider than the card after a /, as the subtitle of a stage's description already did, since a stage folder writes the stage's key twice in its path (packages/bellman/bellman/display/cards.py, _file_block); the cards of cons_savings_iid, sa_savings and retiree_death in the snapshot recordings are written again. A stage's dossier reads the stage files of a period file that no recipe names at stages/<key>/<key>.bl under the period file's folder (packages/bellman/bellman/dossier.py). The refusal of a recipe entry that names no stage file advises the layout's path, stage: stages/<key>/<key>.bl (packages/bellman/bellman/factory/recipe.py), and the example registry of the refusals, REGISTRY_FILES of bellman.refusal_examples, holds its stage file at stages/two_nodes/two_nodes.bl.
  • The recordings that the corpus test compares no longer stand in the model folders under applications/ but with the package's tests (AAS, 2 October 2026: "proceed with the above restructure"). The parsed term <file>.bl.ast.json and the encoding of the elaborated stage <file>.bl.stage.json of a stage file of applications/<model>/ stand in packages/bellman/tests/snapshot/corpus/<model>/: 79 files moved unchanged, among them the specified encoding cons.bl.specified.stage.json of portfolio-choice. The 70 printed parse trees and pages of parsed terms (.tree, .ast.html), which no test or page read, are deleted, and with them every derived/ folder.
  • packages/bellman/tests/snapshot/record.py gains recording_path(stage_path, suffix), the path of a recording, which depends on the application's folder name and the stage file's name alone, and the option --corpus, which writes again, each in the form stored, every recording the corpus test compares and the specified encoding of portfolio-choice/cons.bl, which test_behaviour.py compares; of the stored recordings it leaves out only the parsed term housing-owner/consumption_choice.bl.ast.json, whose stem the corpus test lists as unparseable. packages/bellman/tests/test_snapshot.py checks that every stage file the corpus test collects has its recordings, that every recording belongs to such a file, and that --corpus reproduces each recording it writes byte for byte.
  • The folder packages/bellman/harness/ is retired. Its two modules for the structural tests of the applications, stage_ast.py, the helpers and printers of a parsed term, and stage_types.py, which re-exports the term classes of bellman.syntax.terms, stand in packages/bellman/tests/tools/, from which those tests import them, and parse_stage.py, which wrote the files of the derived/ folders, is deleted. The folder tree of Bellman Workbench no longer leaves out a folder named derived (bellman_workbench/model.py, HIDDEN_NAMES).
  • The forms of Bellman Workbench that write a model folder, new trellis, add stage and add period, which the entry "Bellman Workbench, creating a model and git" below describes, write this layout: a new folder's declaration/ holds the recipe, the trellis and period files, calibration/, settings/ and one folder per stage, stages/<key>/, with the stage file and the methods file its template brings, copied as methods.yml; each row of the recipe writes stage: stages/<key>/<key>.bl; answers.yml, the .gitignore and README.md stand at the folder's top, answers.yml naming a period file by its name in declaration/ and a connector's file by its path from the folder. The templates are read from the moved corpus files cons-port/declaration/trellis.port-cons.yml, cons-port/declaration/trellis.reference-cons-only.yml and pension-retirement/declaration/spec.yml, and a template's model title from economics.md, then README.md. The factory's folder and the recipe's name are two constants of bellman_workbench/model.py, FACTORY_FOLDER and RECIPE, which creation.py imports, so that the Workbench binds a stage from the recipe where new trellis writes it. The tests of these forms and of the classification table, in the Workbench and in the package, that read a moved stage file or the earlier layout read the new paths.
  • Bellman Workbench writes a second trellis of a model in the same folder (AAS, 2 October 2026: "we cannot construct a new trellis in the same folder"). The button new variant, shown where the folder's declaration/ holds spec.yml, asks for a name, a plain word of letters, digits and - such as two-stages, and writes beside the recipe spec.two-stages.yml, trellis.two-stages.yml and period.two-stages.yml: copies of the recipe, of the trellis file it names and of each period file that trellis file names, a period file period.<x>.yml being copied as period.two-stages.<x>.yml, in which the recipe's trellis: and the trellis file's template: entries name the copies and every other line is kept as it stands, comments included (create_variant in bellman_workbench/creation.py, through the new text writer replace_scalar of bellman_workbench/yaml_text.py); the page then opens the variant's recipe. A name that is no plain word, or whose files exist, is refused with a sentence that names the files, before anything is written, and so is the form while a file it copies holds unsaved text. The form add stage offers the period files that the trellis file of spec.yml names, and no longer every period*.yml of declaration/, so that a stage is not added to a variant's period file through spec.yml, after which the factory would refuse both recipes (period_files).
  • Bellman Workbench opened on a folder that holds its recipe spec.yml at its top, as a folder written before this layout does, binds no stage file and says why in the panel: the recipe stands at the folder's top, and the Workbench reads a folder's recipe at declaration/spec.yml (apply_bindings in bellman_workbench/model.py). The notes of the forms add stage and add period name the files each edits by their paths from the model folder: declaration/spec.yml, the period file chosen and answers.yml; or the new period file declaration/period.<label>.yml, declaration/trellis.yml and answers.yml. With a variant's recipe open, the forms thus say that they change the files of spec.yml and none of the variant's.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — Bellman Workbench, the classification table
docs.text:
• Under the text of the open stage file in Bellman Workbench (packages/bellman-workbench/, the page Bellman Workbench §2), three tables headed arvl, dcsn and cntn list the fields at each perch with the declared set as the fields table prints it, the role word and the line of the header that first lists the field; the rows are read from the elaborated stage at every pause. During each reading, the reading each save starts included, and after a reading that makes no stage object (one in the state not parsed, or one in the state parsed, refused in which the construction refused the stage itself), the tables show the last stage that elaborated, dimmed, and take no change (model interface specification 0.3, unit T).
  • A set or a role changed in a cell is written where a header declares the field, in every header that repeats the declaration, as one edit the editor can undo; the box add field writes a new field's declaration into the header that takes it, and a field the file declares elsewhere is read there and left there. In a branching stage the continuation table holds one group per branch, with that branch's fields and the values the elaborated stage types as functions of them; a value whose branch the stage does not answer stands under all branches. The file on disk changes by save alone.
  • The set cells and the code editor expand the Unicode shortcuts of the VS Code extension, read once from editor/dynspec-vscode/snippets/dynspec.json: a prefix such as \StrictlyPositiveReals followed by Tab gives ℝ₊₊. The editor's bundle is rebuilt and its record updated.
  • The package's lowering keeps, after the authored items of the span table that source_spans answers, the place of each side of a block header, each field it lists and each component of the field's typing; bellman.stage exports header_of, branches, to_source, ROLE_WORD and PRIMITIVE_SETS, which the table reads.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — Bellman Workbench, creating a model and git
docs.text:
• Bellman Workbench writes a model from templates: the button new trellis writes a folder in the factory's layout under the folder the Workbench was started on, with the stage files chosen from the application corpus and the files their models bind them with, a recipe whose every binding is an unfilled slot, period.yml, trellis.yml and the form's answers, and opens it with its recipe in the editor; outside a repository the folder is made one with the push destination given. add stage and add period copy one more stage, or write one more period, into such a folder, editing the YAML files as text so that their comments and layout stay. A checklist lists each unfilled slot at its file and line, apart from the refusals, and the tree and the status line count the entries (Bellman Workbench §6).
  • Git's line commits the files of the folder you name, git commit --only, a new file, a deletion and a rename among them, and leaves other staged work as it is; it pushes with the credentials git already holds and shows git's own sentence, a push that would ask for a credential failing at once; and it exports the shown view under model-explorer/ with a record of its inputs' digests and the commit. Nothing is committed on your behalf: the first commit of a new folder is offered, and made when you press commit.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — The trellis, the period file and the recipe in the documentation
docs.text:
• The trellis page docs/Bellman-Sym/07-trelis.md is renamed 07-trellis.md, and every page, lesson, docstring, model note, rule and register that named it is repointed, the three lessons whose opening cell links it recorded again; the records of earlier runs keep the old spelling as they were written.
  • Trellis Syntax is rewritten from AAS's questions of 2 October 2026 on the durables folder, each answer checked against the loaders, and holds the loading of a trellis as it is written and nothing more (AAS, 2 October 2026: everything up to the trellis is about loading a trellis as it is; the overrides and the fills belong to the specification factory). The page explains, in this order, what the three files are for, the trellis file listing the periods and their connectors, the period file a template that binds nothing and the recipe naming each stage's file and its sources by written paths; why the periods are counted backward from the terminal period; the two shapes of a period's stages:, a list of keys read through a recipe and a mapping of records read with none, told apart by the shape and never mixed; how periods are written out one by one, repeated from a template, or both in one list; that a recipe names its trellis file under trellis: and each stage's file under stage:, every path relative to its own folder with nothing assumed, the recipe file being spec.yml and a variant route a second set of the three files beside the first, spec.<name>.yml, trellis.<name>.yml and period.<name>.yml; and how the same trellis is built in Python with accrete and no file. Every example is a file of the corpus or a fragment the loaders accept.
  • The Bellman factory is rewritten to hold the recipe route in full: what a recipe is and what it binds, trellis: and stage: as written paths with the two refusals, the ordered source lists of each kind and the merge in which a later source stands over an earlier one, the slots and the keyword fills of load_recipe and assemble_trellis with the three shapes of a fill, the range lists beside all and periods: [lo, hi], the registry block and the wage schedule written from it, variants side by side, and the route from the recipe to the specified trellis; the construction by accretion is a pointer to the trellis page, and the sections on what each call prints, on what a change makes anew and on the order of a period keep their text and their numbers, every listing run again.
  • Period Syntax, Periods and trellis and the wiki entries Trellis and Period state the two shapes of a period, the template that binds nothing and the names period.yml, spec.yml and period.<name>.yml in the same words.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — The package's names imported from the object they concern
docs.text:
• A public name is imported from the namespace of the object it concerns, the subpackage of bellman named after that object: from bellman.stage import load_stage, elaborate_stage, from bellman.period import period_joins, diagram_period, from bellman.trellis import load_trellis, elaborate_trellis, diagram_trellis, and the four refusal classes from bellman.refusals; the root package bellman exports nothing, so from bellman import load_stage is refused (AAS, 30 September 2026). Each namespace holds one table from each name to the module that defines it, and that module is imported when the name is first used. A function of the view in Model Explorer that takes a stage or a trellis, or reads a view of either, and every constant of the view that the package exports but INITIAL_IDS stand in bellman.stage and in bellman.trellis, one object in two tables; box_attributes and INITIAL_IDS, which concern a stage only, stand in bellman.stage alone. The package's own check of its imports refuses a table entry that names a module which does not define the name. The API index lists the three namespaces in three tables and the stage object in a fourth (The API §2). Every import of a name from bellman in the documentation, the lessons, the tests and the applications is written anew, and the thirteen lessons are recorded again.
  • The package answers what Bellman Workbench computed for itself: source_spans, the source spans of a text, the place of each block, line and top-level item in the file; bind_stage, which binds a stage from the calibration, methods and settings of a source record (Trellis Syntax §6) and reports which of the three binding verbs, calibrate, methodize and configure, it applied, which it skipped because their source was empty, and which refused their source; layers_to_open, the layers a page opens on a view, a layer being a group of the view's nodes, such as those of one builder or one perch, that the viewer draws as one closed box until it is opened (The view in Model Explorer §3.1); node_place, the place of a node of a view, its stage occurrence in a trellis, such as periods[0]/cons, and the block of the stage file whose lines produced it; and wire_counts, the distinct wires of each builders graph, 17 backward and 3 forward for cons.bl. The namespaces also export the names the Workbench still reads that it imported from the package's internal modules: elaborate_text; to_model_explorer, which answers the view as one collection of graphs, the viewer's GraphCollection; method_overlay, which now also takes that collection once it is built; box_attributes; perch_overlays, the three overlays that color a view's wires by their perch; graph_refusal, the refusal held in the place of a graph the construction refused; header_line and source_lines, the line of a block's header and the file and the line number of each line of the stage file that the Source section of a card quotes, the card of a builder (A builder §1), an operation, a block or a definition; BOUNDARY_IDS, the ids of the two nodes, shown as Inputs and Outputs, that hold a builders graph's own inputs and outputs, and LAYER_ID_ENDING, the ending of the id of a layer; INITIAL_IDS, the ids of the graphs of a stage's two initial diagrams; and FAMILY_STYLES and METHOD_TINTS, the fill and border the view gives a node by the family of its operator and the tint of each method tag, which the Workbench's legend shows. Bellman Workbench's model.py imports from no module of the package but the namespaces and bellman.refusals, and defines none of these functions; the lessons' helper opens the layers that layers_to_open names; ConstructionError states that its columns count code points.

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — A recipe writes its paths
docs.text:
• A recipe names every file it reads by its path from its own folder, the registry directory, and nothing is read in place of a path it does not write (AAS, 2 October 2026: "I would like to be explicit about relative paths instead of making assumptions"). The key trellis: at the recipe's top is required, where load_recipe read trellis.yml when the key was absent, and each stage's entry names its stage file under stage:, where the stage key tenure was read from stages/tenure.bl or stages/tenure/tenure.bl. A recipe without trellis: is refused under recipe-shape with the sentence "the recipe names no trellis file; write trellis: trellis.yml, the path from this folder", and an entry without stage: with the sentence "the entry stages.tenure names no stage file; write stage: stages/tenure.bl, the path from this folder", even where the file stands at that path; a written path that names no file, or no .bl file, is refused as load_stage refuses it, under readable-file, at the address stages.tenure.stage (packages/bellman/bellman/factory/recipe.py, stage_record; Refusals §3). The recipe file is named spec.yml, a variant recipe spec.<name>.yml, a variant trellis file trellis.<name>.yml and a variant period file period.<name>.yml (AAS, 2 October 2026: "let's rename spec_factory to spec.yml"); every spec_factory*.yml of the repository is renamed with its readers, and the three lessons that name it are recorded again; the concept keeps its name, the specification factory.
  • Every recipe of the repository writes both keys: the two of applications/durables/, those of applications/pension-retirement/, retirement-choice/, housing-frictions/ and benhabib-2019/, the two of the test corpus and those the tests write; each answers the syntactic trellis it answered before, record for record. The pages that state the recipe's form are corrected (Model directory layout §§1 to 4, Recipe functions §§1 and 2, The Bellman factory §3, Specification factory, the recipe quoted in Retirement choice), and the lessons models/benhabib-2019/the-factory-on-benhabib and topics/branching are recorded again. A stage's dossier reads the stage files of a period file through the recipe whose trellis file names that period file, at the paths the recipe writes, and otherwise beside the period file (packages/bellman/bellman/dossier.py).

docs.title: 2026-10-02 — Bellman Workbench, the Matsya window
docs.text:
• Under the panel of Bellman Workbench stands a window named Matsya, marked by an orange Υ, in which a question typed in words is answered by Matsya, the project's retrieval service over its documents, theory and examples, with the passages the answer rests on, each named by the path the service gives for it (AAS, 1 October 2026). The window opens folded to its bar; a question is sent with ask or the Enter key, in a conversation of the service named after the folder, and the page stays in use while the service answers. The Workbench runs Matsya's own client, the command econ-ark-matsya or matsya, in a separate process and reads the answer it prints; the client keeps the Matsya token and the service's address, which the Workbench never reads, and without the client, or when the service does not answer, the window says so in one sentence (packages/bellman-workbench/bellman_workbench/matsya_client.py and matsya_window.py; Bellman Workbench §5).
  • The method overlay of the view in Model Explorer no longer tints in orange, which the Workbench's page gives to Matsya's mark: a maximization is navy, the solution of an equation a lighter navy and an upper envelope slate, each with a white label (The view in Model Explorer §4.2; packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py).

docs.title: 2026-10-01 — Bellman Workbench, the reviews' corrections
docs.text:
• The graph is read from the file, not drawn by hand, and every box returns to the line that made it; two seconds after the typing stops the picture agrees with the text again, and a wrong line is named by line and column while the last good picture stays. Bellman Workbench (packages/bellman-workbench/, the page Bellman Workbench) now keeps the text typed in one file when another is opened, marks a refusal that follows a mathematical letter such as 𝑢 at the refused text, names the occurrence of the folder's recipe the open file is bound as (periods[0] / worker_saving), and names the state each reading of the text ends in: not parsed, parsed, refused, constructed, forward refused (or backward) or constructed. A stage whose forward graph the construction refuses, entrepreneur_death.bl of the Cagetti–De Nardi model, shows its backward graph and the one node stating the refusal, with the refusal's line and rule in the panel.
  • The status line counts the object and not the drawing: blocks by direction, builders and distinct wires, 20 for cons.bl where the drawing has 21 edges; it prints the seconds the whole reading took and the first characters of the digest of the text and of each bound source. The panel shows, for a box, its rows, its inputs and outputs with the perch defined where it is printed, its kernel and the lines of the file its card quotes as links; for a builder, its signature, parameters and settings; for the graph's own inputs and outputs, the graph's signature; with nothing selected, the stage's sheets. A legend says what the fill and the tint of a box mean, every term on the status line and the panel carries its definition on hover, and the window opens on the folder's first stage file.
  • The two bundles under public/ carry the license notices of what they bundle, and each build record under js/ names its Node version and the digests of its outputs; the editor's bundle rebuilds byte for byte from its sources.
  • Not in this version: the trellis of a folder, the recipe as a table, and git's commit and push from the page.

docs.title: 2026-10-01 — Bellman Workbench, the name and the folder
docs.text: • The browser editor for Bellman-SYM is named Bellman Workbench (AAS, 1 October 2026): the package folder is packages/bellman-workbench/, the module bellman_workbench, the command bellman-workbench <folder>, the environment variables BELLMAN_WORKBENCH_FOLDER and BELLMAN_WORKBENCH_CHROMIUM, the bundle public/codemirror/bellman-workbench.js, and a tab reads <folder> · Bellman Workbench; nothing keeps the former names. The site gains the page Bellman Workbench under Overview, with no menu item of its own.

docs.title: 2026-10-01 — The editor's page after AAS's instructions
docs.text:
• The stage editor of packages/bellman-editor/ (its branch claude/quirky-feynman-pjzz0y) draws the types hidden behind the button hide types by the VS Code extension's rule, wraps the lines at column 78 with a guide, shows the brand's mark, title and favicon, copies the printed card by a button in the panel instead of displaying it, and lists one button per graph of the view's collection, the two initial diagrams first (AAS, 1 October 2026). The status line counts wires over the two builders graphs alone.
  • The file's pane is named Symbolic Bellman and the graph's pane Denotational Semantic Graph (AAS, 1 October 2026); the mark stands at 44 px and the three title bars at the height that holds it.
  • The button horizontal in the graph's bar lays every layer of the graph out left to right through the viewer's own layer configuration (groupNodeConfigs, direction LEFT_RIGHT), and vertical restores the exporter's directions; no change to the exporter or the viewer's build (bellman_editor/model.py, oriented). The viewer's toolbar, whose search box floated over the graph, and its info panel, whose rows the page's panel repeats, and its legend are hidden by its configuration (hideToolBar, hideInfoPanel, hideLegends), so the graph takes the whole region; the graph's buttons stand on a row of their own under the title bar, with zoom in, zoom out and fit, which drive the viewer's own zoom (a wheel event with Ctrl, its space key).
  • The editor's panel answers the nodes of a field diagram, whose fields are the nodes since the exporter's rule of the afternoon of 1 October: a field's rows (kind, perch, role, set, the header line that first lists it), and a click on a field moves the editor to that line; a block of the diagram shows its header, statements and lines and the button that copies its record (bellman_editor/model.py, piece with the collection, node_attributes, header_line_of). The status line and git's line are optional information, hidden behind the button show status (AAS, 1 October 2026), and the server's banner is off.
  • The editor colors a block's id in its header white and bold, the key id= and the header's brackets ice-3, and a statement's annotation from :: to the end of the line ice-3, a marked tag inside it keeping periwinkle, so that the tags read as tags and the ids as the blocks' names (AAS, 1 October 2026); the bundle rebuilt (packages/bellman-editor/js/codemirror/src/bl_language.js, theme.js).

docs.title: 2026-10-01 — The content of the view in Model Explorer
docs.text:
• The view of a stage holds four graphs, listed in the order an author reads them: the two initial diagrams, backward initial diagram and forward initial diagram, in which each block of the stage file is a node on the fields of its header, white, with its header, its statements with their line numbers and its lines as the rows of its side panel, and each field an edge whose ends carry the field's label, perch, role and declared set; then the two builders graphs, backward and forward, as before. explore(stage) and serve with no graph named open on backward, and a trellis holds its two builders graphs alone (packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py; The view in Model Explorer §3.1 and §3.3). AAS asked for the field diagrams in the view on 1 October 2026.
  • The side panel of an operator lists its rows in the order an economist reads them, the kind, the rules, the kernel, the method and the lines; a port writes no row that would hold nothing, so the result of an aggregation, which stands at no perch, lists no perch; the two nodes Inputs and Outputs of a builders graph list the graph's signature as signature() prints it; the method overlay is named method: 1 = !egm, 4 = !Cartesian, the number that stands for each tag written as such, and the viewer's two tables of statistics over those numbers are hidden; a period's layer no longer repeats its index, which its name holds; the reading port of a backward join of a trellis names the rule that paired its wire, paired by; and the node of a refused trellis graph lists each join that leaves a wire unpaired on a row of its own, join 1, join 2, …, with the rules in its refusal (The view in Model Explorer §3.2, §3.3, §4.2 and §5). The study of 30 September proposed two shorter labels, a result wire by the function it carries at its coordinates, 𝑉(m_d), and an aggregation at a policy by 𝐺(𝑐); both change labels the drawing shares, so they wait for AAS behind the module's switch SHORT_LABELS, which defaults to the recorded forms. The content sheet, the design plan and the screenshots stand in AI/dev-specs-briefs/model-interface/spec_0.3/view-content.md and AI/verification/model-explorer/2026-10-01-view-content/.
  • The same evening, at AAS's ruling that the nodes of a field diagram are the fields, each initial diagram is drawn as the field diagram of the calculus is drawn (Fields, functions and types §2). Each perch that holds a field is a layer, arvl, dcsn or cntn, the layers in the order the direction reads them, so that the forward diagram reads arrival, decision, continuation from left to right and the backward one continuation, decision, arrival; each field is a node in the layer of its perch, labeled as the drawing labels it, V≻, m_d, whose side panel lists its kind, its perch, its role, its declared set and the line of the header that first lists it; a shock, which belongs to no perch, stands outside the layers; and each block is a node outside the layers with an edge from each field it reads and into each field it writes. The diagram has no nodes Inputs and Outputs, a field no block writes being one the diagram takes and a field no block reads one it gives, and the ports of the field wires carry no key field, which the afternoon had added so that a page could label the edges: the field's name stands on its node (The view in Model Explorer §3.1 to §3.3; packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py). The screenshots of the two diagrams of cons.bl stand in AI/verification/model-explorer/2026-10-01-field-diagram/.

docs.title: 2026-09-30 — The stage editor, stage A
docs.text:
• An economist starts bellman-editor <folder> on a model folder, and one page in the browser opens on it with four regions: the folder's files with their git marks, the open file in a code editor, the view of the stage's two builders graphs in Model Explorer's browser component, and a panel under the view. Opening a stage file draws its backward graph with the builders as open layers, the node labels as the drawing prints them (𝑉≻ ∘ 𝑔(·, 𝑐) among them); the forward graph is one click away. At every pause of the typing of 750 milliseconds the text is elaborated again, as text and without saving, and the graph redraws from the object the text now denotes, within two seconds for cons.bl. A line the package refuses is marked at its line and column with the package's own sentence, in the editor and in the panel, while the last graph stays drawn, dimmed. A click on a box shows in the panel the box's attributes, its card (denote()) and its kernel (kernel()) character for character and moves the editor to the header of the block that produced the box; the cursor entering a block selects the block's first box in the view and lists the block's boxes in the panel. The status line prints the file's name, the time of the elaboration, the counts of blocks, builders, wires and refusals and the digest of the text; a second line prints git's state of the folder. Saving is explicit, by the Save button or the keyboard's save command; before every save the file's digest is compared with the one remembered, and a file another tool or another tab changed meets the choice compare, overwrite or reload and is overwritten by nothing on its own. This is stage A, reading, the first of the three build stages of the model interface specification 0.2.
  • The code is a distribution of its own, packages/bellman-editor/: bellman_editor/model.py is the module without Solara that the page and the tests read (the folder read as the factory reads it, the buffer elaborated with elaborate_text, the collection and the overlay of the exporter factory/model_explorer.py, the pieces' cards and kernels, the block spans of syntax/lower.py, the bindings of a recipe, the saves under one lock, git as subprocesses); app.py is the Solara page; editor.vue and view.vue are the two Vue 3 components; brand.css holds the site's tokens; command.py is the console command. It is installed editable beside bellman; the viewer package ai-edge-model-explorer is pinned in requirements.txt, with the editor's own pins.
  • Two bundles are served from the package's public/ folder, neither edited by hand. The editor is CodeMirror 6 (codemirror 6.0.2 and its packages, exact versions in js/codemirror/package.json), bundled by Rollup from js/codemirror/src/ into one script, with a tokenizer for .bl files written from the eighteen patterns of the repository's TextMate grammar and the site's code-block palette. The view is Model Explorer's browser component, built from the repository's main branch at the commit 522b7b2 of 11 September 2026 with one patch to the custom element's worker service, whose recipe, patch and build script stand in js/model-explorer/; the published npm package is not used, since it predates the SVG text renderer and the graph fields the exporter writes.
  • The tests are packages/bellman-editor/tests/: test_model.py tests model.py on the corpus stages without Solara, among them that the collection of each corpus stage equals to_model_explorer of the lesson's stage as JSON and that the layers the editor opens equal those the lessons open; test_page.py drives the page in headless Chrome through Playwright, eight tests over the first four acceptance items, against a copy of applications/portfolio-choice/ in a temporary git repository. The page tests are skipped, with the reason printed, where Chromium cannot launch.
  • Not in this stage: the trellis view and the attaching of methods, calibration and settings from the folder (stage B), and the creation of a model from templates, commit and push (stage C). The application's title and headings name PP Monument first and fall back to Archivo, Helvetica and Arial; no font file is copied and no web font is fetched.

docs.title: 2026-09-30 — A record's sources bound by elaborate_stage
docs.text: • elaborate_stage(record) binds the sources the record supplies and answers the bound stage, unless it is given bind=False: a non-empty calibration, a methods mapping whose list methods holds at least one entry and a non-empty settings, in the order calibrate, methodize, configure, each bound as its verb binds it and refused as its verb refuses it, settings without methods among them. An empty source binds nothing, so elaborate_stage(load_stage(path)) and elaborate_text(text, origin) answer the symbolic stage as before, and a bind that is not True or False is refused. The stage is copied once, at the end, where the chain of elaborate_stage and the three verbs copied it four times, and it equals, provenance included, the stage the three verbs make from elaborate_stage(record, bind=False) with the record's mappings. assemble_trellis binds each stage occurrence in the same way and copies it once, 103 copies for the 103 occurrences of the two-stage durables trellis where the calls it stands for made 412, with an equal result, and methodize_trellis copies once a stage occurrence it makes anew (The stage §1; The binding verbs §1). This is AAS's ruling of 30 September 2026, on reading the cell of the parameters lesson that hands elaborate_stage a record with three empty mappings; the lesson gains a cell that hands it the same text with the calibration file read into calibration and prints the calibrated table of parameters, and packages/bellman/tests/test_elaborate_stage_binds.py holds one test for each of the six acceptance items of the brief elaborate-stage-binds-its-record.md.

docs.title: 2026-09-30 — Duplicated code removed
docs.text: • Code written twice now stands once, without a change to what the package answers. The fold reads the operator occurrences of a line with occurrence_paths of packages/bellman/bellman/typing/line_unknowns.py, the walker that also refuses a form no construction rule reads, and its own copy in fold/stage_names.py is removed; stage.par and stage.settings share one base class for their iteration, length, printing and completion (stage/pieces.py); the test of the documentation's shape reads the reference tables with the table reader, the row anchor and the markers of docs/_hooks/reference_pages.py, the script that writes them; the policy card of cons.bl stands once, in packages/bellman/tests/conftest.py, for the two tests that compare it; the per-model tests under applications/ take their spellings, the reading of a stage file, the comparison of two terms and the runner outside pytest from packages/bellman/harness/stage_ast.py; the three figures of applications/cons-port/code/ffp_plots.py share one set-up and one labelling of a panel; and one function each reads the set of a call (fold/declared_sets.py), checks an option keyed by coordinate (stage/binding_verbs.py), prints a clause and rebuilds the parts of a term (typing/typed_expressions.py), makes the pullback row of a value (fold/backward.py) and gathers the conditions of a stage (stage/stage_answers.py).

docs.title: 2026-09-30 — The view of a stage and a trellis in Model Explorer
docs.text:
• A stage version's two builders graphs, and those of a trellis, are read interactively in Model Explorer, Google's viewer of large graphs, which runs in the browser. explore(stage) writes the view as three JSON files into the folder model-explorer/ beside the stage file, serves them from the viewer's server on port 8080, starting one only where none answers there, and opens the page; write_model_explorer(stage, folder) writes the files alone; and serve(graph_path, node_data_path, port=8080, layers=(...)) answers the address of a page on the viewer's server (packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py; The view in Model Explorer). The view is written by functions and by no verb of the stage, as AAS ruled on 29 September: explore and write_model_explorer are exported from bellman, and serve is imported from the module, which stands in factory/ because the view of a trellis reads the joins that factory/joins.py answers. The viewer is the extra explore of the package, pip install -e "packages/bellman[explore]", which installs ai-edge-model-explorer; the core install leaves it out, and without it the module refuses in one sentence naming the extra.
  • In the view each builder is a layer that opens to its sub-builders and its primitive operators, and to no other grain. A primitive operator is a node labeled with the symbol the drawing shows, and the side panel lists its kind, the lines of its kernel, the rows of its card one attribute to a row, the lines of the stage file it realizes, the call that prints its card, and the method bound within it with its handler, options and settings; a layer lists its builder's signature. Every wire is an edge whose two ports hold the wire's identity, its label, its perch, its type and its role. Three edge overlays paint the wires at each perch in the drawing's three perch colors, each edge labeled with the wire's name and the perch's name, V at continuation, and the method overlay tints each operator within which a method is bound, in a tint fixed for each method tag. A direction the construction refused is one node that states the refusal. The view writes no mathematics of its own, and the drawing of diagram() remains the recorded figure of the pages and the lessons.
  • The same day the view took the colors of the project's site, the tokens of docs/_stylesheets/bellman.css, in place of the drawing's: operators filled by family in white and two shades of blue with navy borders and navy labels, layers in pale blue, the three perch overlays in navy, dark orange and blue, the colors the site gives the arrival, decision and continuation perches, and the method overlay tinted by the operation a method realizes, orange for a maximization, the solution of an equation and an upper envelope, and blue for a representation and an expectation. In a lesson, checkout.explore shows the view in a frame under a title line that names the view and its graph and a link to its address (The view in Model Explorer §3.1 and §4).
  • The same evening, at AAS's instruction, the side panel of a primitive no longer lists two attributes, the call that prints its card and the rows of its card's Conditions, and it numbers the lines of a kernel and the rows of a section only where there are several, rule or rule 1 and rule 2. Every port lists the wire's label under label as well, so that an output, which the side panel heads by the node that reads it, shows the wire's label, perch, type and role as an input does. The three perch overlays carry no edge label and are no longer loaded with the view, since the viewer draws an overlay edge as a straight line between two nodes and not along the wire's edge; they stand in the file <label>.edge-overlays.json, which a reader loads through the viewer's panel of edge overlays (The view in Model Explorer §3.2, §3.3 and §4.1).
  • Later that evening, at AAS's instruction, the view was reduced to what a numerical solver, an assistant and an economist need to read a model. A primitive's side panel lists its rules one to an attribute, the region a rule holds on after the rule, 𝑐(𝑚_d≻(a)) = 𝑐≻(a) on 𝑚_d≻(Xa); an evaluation lists only the rows that type its outputs and no rule of the operation before it; and lines names the stage file and the numbers of the lines, cons.bl 22–23. The local abbreviations of the rules, such as the law of motion at a branch, stand once, on the layer of their builder, which also lists each parameter its operations read with its declared set and, on a calibrated version, its value, every setting of a configured version, whether or not a method names it, and on the policy builder's layer the definition of each feasible set its policy names, Γ(x : ℝ₊₊) := (0, x]. The method overlay holds only the graphs within which a method is bound, and the page loads it only then. In a trellis each occurrence's policy ends at a node Outputs inside its layer, and explore(trellis) opens the page located on periods[1], the first period after the terminal one (packages/bellman/bellman/factory/model_explorer.py, packages/bellman/bellman/display/cards.py; The view in Model Explorer §3.3, §4.2 and §5).
  • A trellis is one collection of two graphs, with a layer for each period, periods[h], and for each stage occurrence inside it, periods[h]/<key>, and each join drawn between the wires of the two occurrences it joins, labeled as the drawing of diagram_trellis labels it. The backward graph pairs the marginal values of a join by the coordinates their names declare, through the join's mapping of those coordinates, and otherwise by their role and, where a role holds several, by equal names; where a marginal value is left unpaired, as in the trellises of the pension, durables and housing models, whose names declare no coordinate, the backward graph is refused on one node and the forward graph is drawn.
  • The trial of 30 September, recorded with its notebook and eight screenshots, three of them of the view of the trellis port-cons.yml, in AI/verification/model-explorer/2026-09-30-trial/, found that the viewer's default text renderer garbles the mathematical labels on the canvas while its setting "Use SVG text renderer" draws them exactly, that the side panel draws every attribute exactly with either renderer, that an edge's label is drawn by the older renderer whatever the setting, and that one server serves any number of independent views. These findings fixed the overlays' edge labels in plain letters, with the full label on the port, and the one port, 8080, for which the browser keeps the setting. Seven lessons gain a cell checkout.explore(...) that shows the view in a running kernel; a recorded run of the lessons writes the files and starts no server (tutorials/checkout.py, tutorials/tools/execute_lessons.py).
  • Two questions the build found are filed as issues: the role of a result wire can differ from the role of the field an evaluation makes of it, value for the marginal value m_d ↦ 𝑑𝑢(𝑐(m_d)) of cons.bl (AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/result-role-differs-from-the-evaluated-field.md); and where the names of marginal values declare no coordinate, as in the pension, durables and housing models, nothing the language states pairs two marginal values of different names across a join (AI/road-map/issues-to-be-addressed/marginal-values-paired-by-a-join.md).
  • The tests of packages/bellman/tests/cat/test_model_explorer.py state the view of cons.bl against its builders graphs and its wire table, the kernels and the method attributes against the cards, the overlays, the three files loaded through the viewer's own data classes, the view of the trellis applications/cons-port/trellises/port-cons.yml and the refusal of the pension trellis's backward graph.

docs.title: 2026-09-30 — Homepage and documentation design
docs.text:
• The About us page introduces the project, its authors, support and ways to contribute. It is linked from the homepage footer and the documentation navigation.
  • The homepage introduces Project Bellman with modular loop artwork and links to the existing guides. The documentation uses the same ultramarine, ice and orange palette, logo and typography, with light and dark appearances and layouts for small screens. The documentation's content and page addresses are unchanged.
  • Language contains the user guide, API, appendices and reference catalogues. The API retains its factory and stage-object groups; the sidebar opens the current page's branch and lets readers expand the other groups. Overview and Foundations use the same names as the homepage, and the unemployment example's two existing pages now appear together under Examples.

docs.title: 0.02, the internal developer release
docs.text:
• The second internal release gathers two units built in parallel after the tag internal-dev-0.01: the four document properties on every markdown file, and the builders reached by the pair of perches they join; each adds its dated entry below when it merges.
