    method: !marginals
    block: cons_egm.bl
  - on: cntn_to_dcsn.evaluate.marginal
    method: !Linear
    settings: {grid: !Cartesian, orders: {m: n_m}, bounds: {m: [m_min, m_max]}}

The block file cons_egm.bl beside it opens with the line @methods: cons, defines marginal utility and its inverse in closed form, and holds one block of each kind; the stage's decision state is m, its continuation state a:

@methods: cons
𝑑𝑢(c : ℝ₊₊) := c^(-ρ)
𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑛𝑣(x : ℝ₊₊) := x^(-1/ρ)


[id=egm, (V[>] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !cntn -> (c : ℝ₊₊ @ !ctrl) : !dcsn] {
    c[>]   <= 𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑛𝑣(D_{a}V[>]) ⟂ a >= 0    :: [id=InvEuler]
    m[>]   = a + c[>]                        :: [id=grid]
    c      = c[>]                            :: [id=identification]
}






[id=dcsn_marginal, (c) : !cntn -> (V) : !dcsn] {
    D_{m}V = 𝑑𝑢(c)                           :: [id=envelope]
}

The first entry binds !egm on the policy builder with the block egm, which writes the three lines of §1.1 with its candidate line as the inequality c[>] <= 𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑛𝑣(D_{a}V[>]) ⟂ a >= 0 (Constraints §4.3), and names the exogenous grid of savings at which the candidate line is evaluated, the settings n_a, a_min and a_max (§3). Its header lists the value it reads and the control it writes, and nothing else; the derivative of the continuation value is read by the term, and the header lists nothing for it. methodize elaborates the block with the stage's declarations and the block file's own definitions in scope, and its lines become the policy builder's method rows, the operations of that builder in stage.builder. The initial diagrams keep the stage file's maximization, and so do the builders as the stage file states them, which stage.declared reads by the same keys as stage.builder. The stage records the condition under which the method rows reach the declared maximization, and stage.obligations() lists it under the name egm-eligibility; nothing checks it.

The block reads the derivative of the continuation value by the term D_{a}V[>] and declares nothing about how it is evaluated: the stage that built that value fixed it, and this block knows only that the value it reads is a function. The second entry binds !marginals on the decision value builder with the block file's marginal block, a block whose lines are derivative lines, each stating a derivative of the value the builder writes as the author asserts it: the envelope condition D_{m}V = 𝑑𝑢(c), the derivative of the decision value in cash on hand. Its header is the builder's header restricted to what its line reads, the control c and the value V. methodize records the line at the builder's closing Evaluation, beside the representation method bound there, as a stated derivative of the value by coordinate, with the line's id and its source; the builder's signature is unchanged, no wire and no box is added, and the value's record lists the coordinate m under derivatives. The reading of the line as the derivative of the value rests on the envelope conditions; stage.obligations() lists it under marginal-reading and nothing checks it.

How the derivative of a value is evaluated is a property of the value, fixed here, in the methods file of the stage that writes it, in one of two ways: by the stated line, whose values the representation at the builder's Evaluation stores beside the value's; or, where no line states the derivative, by the representation of the value itself, where its method's row says it evaluates the derivative (Method types, the column derivatives it evaluates). The methods file writes that representation at the builder's Evaluation, by the value, cntn_to_dcsn.evaluate.value, or by the stated derivative, cntn_to_dcsn.evaluate.marginal, as the third entry binds !Linear on the grid of resources its setting grid names; the two addresses name one Evaluation, which holds one representation method (§4). A later stage whose block reads D_{a}V[>] of this stage's value receives the derivative so fixed and declares nothing (Trellises §2.1). The demonstration's consumption stage declares no arrival perch: its decision value is the value the stage exports, and its decision state m is where the trellis joins the stage before it. A stage with an arrival builder whose law between the perches is the identity, V[<] = V or V[<] = E_{y}V, writes no derivative line on it, since the stored derivative values pass through the same map; where the pass-through crosses an expectation the package lists the condition that the derivative of the expectation is the expectation of the derivative, as differentiation-under-the-integral, and checks nothing. Where the law is not the identity, the author writes the arrival derivative line with the law's factor, as the buffer-stock model writes D_{k}V[<] = E_{ψ,ξ}(R*(Γ*ψ)^(-ρ)*D_{m}V). Nothing is differentiated: the package computes no derivative that no line states and no representation evaluates. A stage file whose value builder writes the derivative line itself, as cons_interior.bl of §1.1 does, needs no marginal block. Expression forms §4 gives the two forms of a block file.

docs.title: 5 Loading and attaching choices
docs.text:
Stages are written in .bl; the three attachment files remain YAML:

Source Contents cons.bl Declarations, typed blocks, equations, and shock laws. methodization.yml Computation targets, method tags, and references to settings. settings.yml Values for numerical settings. calibration.yml Economic parameter values.

For cons.bl, use the recognition-only methodization.yml in §1 and supply settings.yml as an empty mapping and calibration.yml with ρ: 2. The sequence is:

from bellman.stage import elaborate_stage, load_stage

stage = elaborate_stage(load_stage("cons.bl"))
calibrated = stage.calibrate("calibration.yml")
methodized = calibrated.methodize("methodization.yml")
specified = methodized.configure("settings.yml")

Loading reads the file into a source record, and elaboration constructs the initial stage from it, with no methods, settings, or calibration attached. Each subsequent operation adds its binding to the stage it is called on and returns that stage, so calibrated, methodized and specified name one stage (The binding verbs). The recommended order shown above puts calibration first and configuration last. The package also accepts methodization followed by calibration and configuration, or methodization followed by configuration and calibration. It refuses configuration before methodization because the chosen methods determine which settings are needed. Calibration supplies parameter values without replacing the symbolic equations. These three accepted orders prepare the same specified stage; with recognition-only methods they supply no maximization algorithm and do not solve the model. For the interior example, substitute cons_interior.bl and cons_interior_methods.yml, with settings appropriate to that method.

Duplicate method targets, unknown method tags and unresolved targets are errors. A refusal names the entry and the stage's available places. Methodization also refuses a missing required option or an option the method does not admit, except for an untyped option owned by a named handler. Configuration requires a methodized stage, values for every required option reference and values satisfying the option types and joint conditions. Calibration requires every declared parameter and binds only declared parameter names. Extra supplied settings remain in the settings mapping, but do not become declarations.

The queries below inspect the three public parts of this process without executing a numerical routine:

from bellman.stage import method_types

print(method_types["!Linear"])
print(calibrated.places())
print(specified.settings)

Each method_types entry displays its admitted places and typed options. places() lists the addresses and kinds available on this stage (Methods and places). settings lists each setting value and, for every method that reads it, the place under read at, the method under by and, where the setting is a field of the method's grid, the grid's kind under grid (Parameters and settings). A setting that no method reads remains listed with no reader.

The Bellman factory applies the same sequence to each stage occurrence of a trellis, meaning one stage file elaborated at one position of a period (Periods). Repeated stage occurrences have independent graphs and specifications; that independence does not imply that lifecycle operations can be applied in any order.

docs.title: 6 Candidate consumption and interpolation
docs.text:
In the separate interior example in §1.1, c[>] is candidate consumption indexed by savings, and m_d[>] is its associated cash on hand. The equation c = c[>], interpreted through a = m_d-c, constrains the unknown consumption choice. It does not assert that every numerical root maximizes value.

For the displayed power utility, use strictly positive consumption and ρ > 1, for example ρ = 2; then inverse marginal utility is defined on strictly positive, finite continuation marginal values. Interior optimality uses the Euler condition and the relevant differentiability assumptions. The borrowing boundary needs its own declared feasible choice and optimality conditions. In particular, a constrained policy requires the Kuhn–Tucker condition in one of its three spellings, the clause ⟂ m_d - c >= 0 on the decision-perch first-order condition, using the forward law a = m_d - c, a multiplier declared in the policy block, or the clause ⟂ a >= 0 on the continuation-marked candidate line c[>] <= 𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑛𝑣(D_{a}V[>]) (Constraints §4), or a declared constrained branch, or a restriction of the implicit equality to the interior with the constrained branch declared separately. With the clause on the candidate line the corner belongs to the relation the file states. At zero saving the candidate takes every value up to the interior value, and the identification, the last line c = c[>] (Field equations §3), gives consumption equal to cash on hand there; a method attached at the Evaluation therefore takes the corner's pairs, which the clause declares, beside the pairs of its grid (Constraints §4.3). A handler adding a boundary segment to a block that states none of these must report it as an extension outside the declared equality; see Appendix C §4.5, which also states when the three spellings define one policy and when that policy is the maximizer. This modular consumption stage contains no discount factor: when composed with a separate discounting stage, the continuation value and its derivative already include that stage's discounting.

More generally, candidate coordinates and controls define a relation: a set of state–control pairs. They define one control on the candidate state domain exactly when candidates with equal coordinates have equal controls. A policy on the intended domain additionally needs coverage of that domain and appropriate measurability. If several controls occur at one state, a selection must be supplied. Comparing candidate values establishes the true optimum only if the candidate family includes the relevant feasible optima and a maximum is attained. Appendix C R10 and R12 state these conditions.

A numerical method may interpolate candidate pairs internally. An explicitly authored evaluate(knots, values, x) is optional: it is a separate mathematical operation with declared inputs and its own approximation conditions. Naming an interpolation method does not insert that equation into the stage. Nor does internal upper-envelope selection, which compares candidate values at a common state, create a separately authored upper_env target.

A numerical grid is a finite collection of points for approximating a function on its declared domain. It does not replace that domain. A simulation grid may differ from the grid used to solve the model; the numerical routine must specify how its representations are related.

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
#branching

Summary

A branching stage describes a discrete choice, or a draw by nature, with a separate continuation state for each alternative. We declare the choice labels, write each branch's continuation fields in its own labeled block, and select from the branch values in the order of the labels. The label is the stage's only control; a continuous choice made under one alternative is a stage of its own on that branch. The retirement example below distinguishes the value of a supplied choice from the policy that chooses the better alternative.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Stages and Field equations: declarations, signatures, and equations. Used by — Periods: connecting each branch to its successor; Trellises: connecting periods. Formal account — Branching and Appendix C: branch values and selection assumptions.

docs.title: 1 Work or retire
docs.text:
This complete stage file is the retirement choice of the retirement application, applications/retirement-choice/declaration/stages/ret_choice/ret_choice.bl. Assets are unchanged by the choice itself; the two alternatives have separately named continuation assets and values. The parameter δ is the positive utility cost of working.

@stage: ret_choice

δ : ℝ₊₊          :: ["utility cost of working, charged in the period whose wage it earns"]

[id=arvl_to_dcsn, (a : ℝ₊) : !arvl -> (a_d : ℝ₊) : !dcsn] {
    a_d = a                                   :: [id=assets]
}

[id=dcsn_to_cntn, (a_d, d : !ctrl @ {work, retire}) : !dcsn -> ()] {
    [label=work,   () -> (a_w : ℝ₊) : !cntn] { a_w = a_d }
    [label=retire, () -> (a_r : ℝ₊) : !cntn] { a_r = a_d }
}

[id=cntn_to_dcsn, (V_w[>] : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu, V_r[>] : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu, d) : !cntn -> (V : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu) : !dcsn] {
    V = (V_w[>] - δ, V_r[>])[d]                   :: [id=choice_value]
}

[id=dcsn_to_arvl, (V) : !dcsn -> (V[<] : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu) : !arvl] {
    V[<] = V                                  :: [id=value]
}

[id=policy, (V_w[>], V_r[>]) : !cntn -> (d : {work, retire} @ !ctrl) : !dcsn] {
    d = argmax_{d}(V_w[>] - δ, V_r[>])        :: [id=choice]
}

The derivative of the choice value in assets is not written in the stage file. It stands in the stage's block file, applications/retirement-choice/declaration/methods/marginals_ret_choice.bl, as a marginal block, a block of derivative lines that the stage's methods file binds on the decision builder with !marginals (Methodization §4.1):

@methods: ret_choice
# The derivative of the value of the discrete choice in assets, stated by the
# marginal block of the decision value builder: the derivative of the branch
# value the choice d selects; the cost of work, a constant, contributes nothing.

[id=dcsn_marginal, (V_w[>], V_r[>], d) : !cntn -> (V) : !dcsn] {
    D_{a_d}V = (D_{a_w}V_w[>], D_{a_r}V_r[>])[d]  :: [id=marginal]
}

The control d takes labels from {work, retire}. The two nested blocks, labeled work and retire, define a_w and a_r. No kind: branching YAML header is needed: the typed discrete control and the branch blocks declare the alternatives.

In the value equation, (V_w[>] - δ, V_r[>])[d] selects the value for a supplied choice. The first component corresponds to work, and the second to retire. The derivative line of the marginal block, D_{a_d}V = (D_{a_w}V_w[>], D_{a_r}V_r[>])[d], states the derivative of the value in assets as the derivative of the selected branch's value, in the same order; the cost of working does not depend on assets, so it has no counterpart there. The policy equation's argmax over (V_w[>] - δ, V_r[>]) is read as that same tuple indexed by d: the policy chooses a label whose entry is largest. The two tuples agree entry by entry and in order. A policy that writes them in another order would select a label using the wrong payoff, and the stage is refused under the rule branch-tuple-mismatch (Refusals).

The parameter δ is charged on the working alternative once. Discounting, earnings, and subsequent consumption are not additional computations in this choice stage; they belong in whichever stages supply its continuation values.

The label is the only control of a branching block. A continuous choice that the agent makes under one alternative, consumption after choosing to work, is a stage of its own on that alternative's branch, and the period connects the branch to it: the retirement application's period.yml lists ret_choice, then worker_cons and retiree_cons; its connector joins a_r to the retiree's arrival field a_ret, and a_w joins the worker's arrival field of the same name (Periods). A paper that writes the two choices as one maximization over the pair, as the retirement model's Bellman equation does with consumption and next period's status, is stated in this language as the maximization over the label of the values the consumption stages supply; the iterated maximization equals the joint one wherever the inner maximum exists. A branching block that lists a continuous control beside its label is not constructed, and the stage holds a refusal under not-constructed (Refusals); §4 states the same rule for a branch drawn by nature.

Alternatives that all lead to the same successor stage are not branches. A household choosing among J cities faces the same problem next period whichever city it chooses: the choice is an integer control j : L_J @ !ctrl over the city set L_J := {1, …, J}, and one block with no labels retains the chosen city as the integer continuation state, i_n = j; the cities' payoffs and distances are indexed data, δ[j] and dist[j][i] (Stages §2.1). The number of alternatives then remains a parameter, which a branching block cannot admit, since it holds one labeled block for each member of a finite set of names. An alternative whose continuation problem differs from the others', an outside option with a state of its own, is a branch of a branching stage, and the choice among the remaining alternatives is a stage of its own on that branch.

docs.title: 2 Branch states and values
docs.text:
The continuation state space is a disjoint union of the branches' state spaces: each continuation state is a state of one branch together with that branch's label. Thus a working state consists of work and its a_w, while a retired state consists of retire and its a_r. Both asset fields have nonnegative-real domains, but they remain distinct branch fields.

This differs from a pair of simultaneous asset holdings. Even where alternatives share a common continuous domain, the branch label remains necessary to distinguish their continuation problems; where every alternative has the same continuation problem, there is no branch, and the chosen alternative is an integer state (§1). A value function on the disjoint union is equivalently a family of value functions, one on each branch. In this example, V_w[>] and V_r[>] are the separately declared value fields representing that family.

Ordinary brackets select a collection entry: the [d] in §1 selects a tuple component. The [>] in V_w[>] identifies the continuation information set. These uses of brackets have different meanings; see Equation parsing rules.

docs.title: 3 Choosing an alternative
docs.text:
The value equation gives the payoff conditional on d. The argmax equation constrains d to an alternative attaining the largest payoff. The block identifiers cntn_to_dcsn and policy are descriptive addresses; the selection and maximization expressions specify the mathematical operations.

For the two finite, real-valued alternatives in §1, a maximum exists at each state where both values are defined. If the two values coincide, both labels maximize value. A numerical implementation needs a stated tie-breaking rule to return one control. A measurable policy requires measurable branch values and a suitable selection; an arbitrary tie rule is not a substitute for that requirement. If some alternatives are infeasible at a state, the admissible choice set must express that restriction.

The example states a deterministic discrete choice. A stochastic choice model needs its own declared probability law and equations; §4 gives the form. A probability-weighted value, an expectation, and an optimal discrete choice are different operations; a method tag does not supply one in place of another.

When the package constructs the stage from this file, the forward block dcsn_to_cntn keeps one law of motion, the map from the decision state and the label to the continuation state, and each branch reads it at its own label. The section of the law at a label is the law with d fixed at that label: the section at work, printed 𝑔_work≻, sends decision assets to a_w, and the section at retire, printed 𝑔_retire≻, sends them to a_r. The decision builder evaluates each branch's continuation value at the assets its own section gives, 𝑉_w≻ ∘ 𝑔_work≻ for work, forms the tuple of the value equation, and selects its entry at the policy; the policy builder's Argmax row, choice:Argmax, chooses a label that maximizes the same tuple. Forward, the policy splits the distribution of agents at the decision perch into one distribution for each label: the agents who choose work are carried along the work section to a_w, and those who choose retire to a_r, and the two masses add up to the mass at the decision perch. Each builder's card, what denote() prints (A builder §1), states the sections once, under the heading Where. The mathematics of a branching stage is in Branching.

docs.title: 4 A branch drawn by nature
docs.text:
A retiree in the model of Cagetti and De Nardi (2006, "Entrepreneurship, Frictions, and Wealth", Journal of Political Economy 114, Section III.A) survives the year or dies and leaves the assets to an offspring. The stage file applications/cagetti-denardi-2006/declaration/stages/retiree_death/retiree_death.bl declares the draw and its law:

s : {survive, die}
s ~ Categorical((π_o, 1 - π_o))                                             :: ["surviving or dying, with probabilities in the order of the labels"]

and writes the two branches and the value line:

[id=dcsn_to_cntn, (a, y, θ, s) : !dcsn -> ()] {
    [label=survive, () -> (a_rd_rt : Xa) : !cntn] {
        a_rd_rt = a
    }
    [label=die, () -> (a_rd_yc : Xa, y_rd_yc : Y, θ_rd_yc : Θ) : !cntn] {
        a_rd_yc = a
        y_rd_yc = y
        θ_rd_yc = θ
    }
}

[id=cntn_to_dcsn, (W_r[>] : ℝ @ !vlu, V_young[>] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !cntn -> (V : ℝ @ !vlu) : !dcsn] {
    V = β*E_{s}((W_r[>], η*V_young[>])[s])       :: [id=value]
}

The shock s takes the labels {survive, die}, and its law gives each label its probability in the order of the labels, π_o to survive and 1 − π_o to die. No policy block chooses the label. The value line takes the expectation over s of the tuple indexed by s: the value is the sum of the branch values weighted by the law, 𝑉 = β · (π_o · 𝑊_r≻ + (1 − π_o) · η · 𝑉_young≻), each branch value read at the state its own section gives. The decision builder's card prints the line's rule in the form the file writes it, the expectation over s of the tuple indexed by s, with each branch value read at its own section; the definition of its aggregation states the weighted sum. Forward, the distribution at the decision perch is extended by the law of s, and the households drawn at each label are carried along that label's section; the two masses add up to the mass at the decision perch. This file's forward builders are refused for another reason: the offspring's abilities are drawn from the family Invariant, which the package does not admit, and worker_ageing.bl, the aging of a worker in the same model, shows the forward builder of a draw. A law that selects branches gives each label one probability: Categorical with one weight per label, or Bernoulli(p) over two labels, which gives the second label the probability p. A branching block is constructed when its branches state equations alone and the label that selects a branch is either the block's one control or a shock over a finite set in a stage that chooses nothing; a stage that draws its branch and also chooses a control is refused under the rule not-constructed, and Refusals lists the rules of a malformed draw.

A branch on which the model ends, death without an heir, keeps the continuation state its terminal value reads, the assets at death, and the value line reads a continuation value for that branch as it does for die above. In the terminal period that value comes from a stage that lists V[>] in its backward header and reads it, as the bequest stage of the retirement application does, applications/retirement-choice/declaration/stages/bequest/bequest.bl; the user supplies the function when the model is realized, zero where the paper gives no bequest value (Trellises §2). Death does not set that value to zero by itself, and a zero value does not require removing the branch's field: the language has no empty branch, and a branch that writes no continuation field is refused under branch-form.

docs.title: 5 Connecting the branches
docs.text:
A period connects each continuation branch to the appropriate successor stage. In §1 those fields are a_w and a_r. The branches share one stage's field namespace, so these distinct states have distinct names. A working successor can declare arrival assets a_w, and a retirement successor can declare arrival assets a_r. Each name belongs to its own stage; the package infers a connection only when it is the unique compatible, globally consistent choice among eligible continuation and arrival uses.

An authored connector can select corresponding fields whether their names agree or differ. Use a bare name when its eligible endpoint is unique and a stage-key prefix where the name is ambiguous. A pair must pass the declared-set check; the author must also establish its economic meaning, units and information at the join. It does not compute returns or change units. The full rules are in Periods.

The branch identity must remain unambiguous throughout this matching. Distinct names alone do not prove that all declared joins are compatible, and shared domains alone do not identify a successor. Do not infer a branch route merely from the order of the stages in the period file.

Whether retirement is absorbing is determined by the subsequent stages and inter-period connections. The choice stage alone does not prevent a future return to work. Trellises explains how the retired continuation can remain connected to retired stages across periods.

docs.title: 6 Numerical methods
docs.text:
A method can attach to the authored policy builder, a supported named !node, or a supported operator occurrence. For §1, on: argmax applies to every argmax in the stage; on: policy.choice.argmax overrides that choice for the named statement. This attachment does not make the statement another authored node. Methodization gives the address rules.

Neither the discrete control nor its labels create an upper_env equation. If a continuous-choice algorithm generates several candidates per branch, its candidate-selection and interpolation requirements must be stated in that algorithm's mathematical and numerical contracts; see Methodization.

docs.title: Period Syntax
docs.text:
Summary

A period is a collection of stage occurrences and the connections between their fields. We keep this outer description in YAML and write the stage files in .bl. Field dependencies determine the order of computation; the order of names in the stage list does not. The period file is a template that a trellis file repeats: written as a list of stage keys it binds nothing, and a recipe supplies each stage's file and values; written as a mapping from each key to a record, it carries them itself (Trellises §3).

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Stages: typed fields and stage files; Branching: separate continuation alternatives. Used by — Trellises: ordering periods; The Bellman factory: loading, elaborating and binding every stage occurrence of a trellis. Formal account — Periods and the trellis: composition through compatible fields.

docs.title: 1 Period YAML
docs.text:
The household observes resources, consumes, and invests its remaining assets before next period's income and return are drawn. We express this sequence with the beta-free cons.bl from Field equations and the disc.bl and port.bl sources below. The discount stage multiplies value by beta, while its asset transition is an identity. It adds no economic decision.

Save this period template as period.yml:

!period
name: consumption_investment
stages:
  - cons
  - disc
  - port
connectors:
  - {k_next: k}

The recipe beside the template associates each key with its stage file, stage: cons.bl, and with the files of its parameter values, settings and methods (Trellises §§1, 5); the template itself binds nothing. Consumption's outgoing a and discounting's incoming a are different fields; their compatible, uniquely selected same-name pair connects them. The authored connector pairs discounting's outgoing k_next with investment's incoming k. The period begins with observed resources m and ends with next resources m_next; their join across periods is kept outside this file.

Key Contents name A documentation label for the period template. stages A list of distinct stage-occurrence keys, or a mapping from each key to a record that names its stage file and its bindings (Trellises §3). connectors A list of authored pairs from continuation state fields to arrival state fields; paired names may agree or differ.

A stage occurrence is one use of a stage file in a period: the file elaborated at that position, with its own field names, methods and settings. A parameter name declared by two stages of one period denotes one shared period parameter; it need not have the same value in another period. A stage key identifies that use; the file's declared name remains its .name, the same for every stage occurrence of the file, and may differ from an application-supplied key, and the position is recorded in the occurrence's provenance. Missing or duplicate keys are errors. Repeating a stage file requires distinct stage-occurrence keys, not repeated list entries with the same key.

A stage's source is a .bl file, named by the recipe under stage: or by a record under the same key, or in-memory text with an explicit origin (Trellises §6). No stage is written inline in the template, which remains YAML and describes the outer composition only, separately from the grammar of the statements inside a .bl stage.

docs.title: 1.1 Discounting
docs.text:
Save the following value-only stage as disc.bl. Both asset boundaries are nonnegative and measured in the same units. This example calls its outgoing assets k_next to distinguish the next investment input. A distinct name is not required to avoid automatic matching: selection considers eligible fields, their stage addresses, compatibility and the whole period's dependencies. The position of investment relative to the period boundary is stated by its connector.

@stage: disc
β : (0,1)
[id=arvl_to_dcsn, (a : ℝ₊) : !arvl -> (a_d : ℝ₊) : !dcsn] {
    a_d = a
}
[id=dcsn_to_cntn, (a_d) : !dcsn -> (k_next : ℝ₊) : !cntn] {
    k_next = a_d
}
[id=cntn_to_dcsn, (V[>] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !cntn -> (V : ℝ @ !vlu) : !dcsn] {
    V = β*V[>]
}
[id=dcsn_to_arvl, (V) : !dcsn -> (V[<] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !arvl] {
    V[<] = V
}

The backward equation discounts the supplied continuation value once. Consumption itself contains no beta. This variant omits the marginal-value output in applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/disc/disc.bl and gives outgoing assets a distinct name; it is the source used on this page.

docs.title: 1.2 Investment
docs.text:
Save this stage as port.bl. The household chooses its risky share ς in [0,1] before observing either the risky gross return Ψ or next income θ. The safe gross return is R. Both shocks are positive, so next resources are positive even when capital is zero.

For each shock, log values are normal with the displayed mean and standard deviation. In addition, we specify the ordered joint conditional law

\[ K(d\psi,d\theta)=\nu_\Psi(d\psi)\nu_\theta(d\theta), \]

constant given investment-decision information, where \(\nu_\Psi\) and \(\nu_\theta\) are the two lognormal laws. This states both independence between the shocks and independence of their joint draw from earlier observations. The two marginal declarations in the source do not encode that additional joint-law assumption; it accompanies this example.

@stage: port
R : ℝ₊₊
μ_Ψ : ℝ
σ_Ψ : ℝ₊
μ_θ : ℝ
σ_θ : ℝ₊
Ψ : ℝ₊₊
θ : ℝ₊₊
Ψ ~ LogNormal(μ_Ψ, σ_Ψ)
θ ~ LogNormal(μ_θ, σ_θ)
[id=arvl_to_dcsn, (k : ℝ₊) : !arvl -> (k_d : ℝ₊) : !dcsn] {
    k_d = k
}
[id=dcsn_to_cntn, (k_d, ς : [0,1] @ !ctrl, Ψ, θ) : !dcsn -> (m_next : ℝ₊₊) : !cntn] {
    m_next = k_d*(ς*Ψ + (1-ς)*R) + θ
}
[id=cntn_to_dcsn, (V[>] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !cntn -> (V : ℝ @ !vlu) : !dcsn] {
    V = E_{Ψ,θ}(V[>])
}
[id=dcsn_to_arvl, (V) : !dcsn -> (V[<] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !arvl] {
    V[<] = V
}
[id=policy, (V[>]) : !cntn -> (ς) : !dcsn] {
    ς = argmax_{ς}(E_{Ψ,θ}(V[>]))
}

For capital \(k\geq0\) and share \(s\in[0,1]\), next resources are \(M(k,s,\Psi,\theta)=k(s\Psi+(1-s)R)+\theta\). Given a continuation function \(v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) of next resources, the portfolio objective is \(E[v(M(k,s,\Psi,\theta))]\). Assume it is finite, jointly measurable in capital and share, and continuous in the share; select a measurable maximizer. Continuity on the compact share interval then gives attainment. Continuous \(v\) with a suitable integrable bound can justify the required expectation continuity; finite pointwise expectations alone do not.

At zero capital every share gives resources θ; choose share zero there. The operative argmax includes both share endpoints, unlike an interior first-order equation. This documented variant also admits zero capital and uses positive shocks with the joint law above. The repository's applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/port/port.bl declares the joint law as one lognormal declaration with correlation ρ_ζ and continues to m_next, as here. A no-risky-asset variant fixes the share to zero and removes its policy and unused return-shock declarations; it still uses the same nonnegative-capital and positive-resource boundaries.

docs.title: 2 Connectors
docs.text:
A connector selects eligible continuation and arrival state fields for a stage join. In the main period, the outgoing field is written first and the incoming field second:

connectors:
  - {k_next: k}

The declared boundaries explain which connections are within the period and which are left for its successor. A stage's local field name does not identify a field in another stage:

Join Domains and units Where it is specified cons.a to disc.a Nonnegative assets in the same units. Unique compatible same-name selection within the period. disc.k_next to port.k Nonnegative assets in the same units. {k_next: k} within the period. port.m_next to the next cons.m Strictly positive resources in the same units. {m_next: m} between periods.

The stage declarations establish direction. Reversing the pair is not another spelling of the same join. The second authored pair belongs in the inter-period connector, not alongside the first: placing both in this period would close a cycle.

The pair performs no calculation. Interest, income, depreciation, discounting, and unit conversion must appear in a stage equation. Equal domain labels alone do not establish compatibility: the fields must denote compatible quantities with matching economic roles and information at the join. Their continuation and arrival tags refer to different stages, but describe the same boundary information after identification. Perch tagging rules explains why tags within a stage do not by themselves identify quantities across stages.

For a field with category codes, a connection checks both the admissible integers and their recorded meanings. Every code the preceding stage can write must be accepted by the receiving stage with the same meaning. This applies to authored pairs, inferred pairs and connections between periods, and to each coordinate of a product. A domain with category meanings is incompatible with an ordinary integer domain that records none.

For example, two stages using the identifier household_status with newborn=0, old=1 can copy their status fields. If the receiving stage instead declares newborn=1, old=0, copying 0 would change its meaning, so the connection is marked incompatible. A stage equation such as n_next = 1 - n can express the required conversion into that reversed coding; a connector performs no conversion, and the package does not prove that an arbitrary transition preserves category meanings. The identifier and its scope are described in Symbol conventions §9.2.2.

A restriction of a coded set retains the meanings of its admitted codes. For example, Old := {j : HouseholdStatus | j = 1} admits only old households under the preceding coding. A field on Old can be copied into one on HouseholdStatus, but the reverse is marked incompatible because HouseholdStatus also admits newborn households.

Technical details

Literal conditions such as j >= 1 or j = 1 determine which codes a restriction admits. If another condition, such as one naming a parameter, leaves its members undetermined, a connection whose answer depends on those members is not established. This includes a connection into that restriction, and a connection out of it into a set with disagreeing meanings, since the restriction may be empty. Within one period the same restriction on both sides is one set when its conditions use numbers and parameters; a condition that calls a function leaves even that connection unestablished.

For indexed collections, a connection requires matching keys in the same order as well as compatible entry domains. Thus collections on {0, θ} ⊂ ℤ and {θ, 0} ⊂ ℤ cannot be copied directly, even at the same value of θ. A stage equation must express any reordering of their entries.

An authored connector selects one eligible continuation use and one eligible arrival use. Write {k_next: k} when each endpoint name is unique on its side of the period; if either name occurs at more than one eligible stage, prefix that endpoint with its stage key, as in {disc.k_next: port.k}. The prefix is an address, not a change to the stage's equation. Authored pairs are considered before automatic same-name inference and claim their endpoints. Automatic inference selects only a uniquely compatible, globally consistent pair; an unresolved candidate is not a connection. The package checks declared sets, while the author must establish economic meaning, units and information. Reused value names inside different stages remain local; they are not an instruction to identify all value fields in the period. On branches, preserve the branch-specific field names and route each declared continuation to the intended successor. The retirement stage, for example, distinguishes a_w from a_r.

Selecting field pairs does not yet establish a complete stage connection. A route is the selected pairing of one complete ordered continuation state with one complete ordered arrival state. The package checks every coordinate, the declared treatment of branches and any required joint law, and the value and derivative components passed backwards. Separate marginal laws do not establish an unspecified joint law. A coordinate exchange reorders the supplied derivative components; it neither differentiates an equation nor changes the stage order.

The connection report distinguishes selected pairs from certified routes and records the parameter bindings used in their checks. A route is certified only when its required conditions are established. An incomplete route, an incompatible component or a condition left undecided remains visible with its reason; none is confirmation of a complete connection. In Workbench, an unresolved authored entry remains in the source with its diagnostic while the model is being edited.

docs.title: 3 Stage order
docs.text:
The stage-dependency graph records which stage supplies fields needed by another. Its directed edges follow the economic direction from continuation to arrival. For the example in §1, consumption precedes discounting and investment in forward time; computing value works backwards through investment, discounting, and consumption.

The list [cons, disc, port] does not define this order. Reordering it leaves the intended connections unchanged. Where independent branches exist, several stages can be ready for computation at once. A within-period cycle has no such backward order and must be rejected for this construction. Boundary fields are those not supplied or consumed by a within-period connection; inter-period joins are described on the next page.

There are three different objects to keep separate:

Object What it represents A stage's semgraph The typed equations and dependencies within one stage, held in four graphs, each a DisCoPy Hypergraph: two initial diagrams on the fields, and two builders graphs, the backward one on value functions and the forward one on distributions. The stage-dependency graph Connections between stage occurrences, used to obtain a permissible computation order. The syntactic trellis The model as written: the methods, settings, and calibration of each stage occurrence, by period index and stage key, held as data.

The first represents the model's mathematical equations, the second its between-stage dependencies, and the third its numerical and parameter assignments. A graph showing an order does not establish that the value functions are measurable, expectations finite, or optima attained; those assumptions remain as in Appendix C.

docs.title: 3.1 Choosing the period boundary
docs.text:
For the main period, let \(v\) be next period's value of positive resources and let \(P_v(k)=\max_{s\in[0,1]}E[v(M(k,s,\Psi,\theta))]\) be investment value. The resulting consumption problem is

\[ C_v(m)=\max_{0<c\leq m}\{u(c)+\beta P_v(m-c)\}. \]

Consumption and the share decision precede the next shock draw. The income realization that produced initial resources is already observed at this period's arrival. In addition to §1.2's conditions, require \(P_v\) to be finite and continuous on compact capital intervals so that the consumption attainment argument applies. Concavity supplies the additional uniqueness and first-order characterizations when those are used.

Alternatively, begin the period before investment and end after consumption and discounting. Save this period template separately as period.investment-first.yml, a variant beside the first (Trellises §5):

!period
name: investment_consumption
stages:
  - port
  - cons
  - disc
connectors:
  - {m_next: m}

Now port.m_next joins cons.m within the period, while disc.k_next joins the next period's port.k through {k_next: k}. The period's arrival and continuation states are nonnegative capital. Its share decision precedes the shocks, but consumption observes the realized resources. Given next-period capital value \(J:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), the period problem is

\[ I_J(k)=\max_{s\in[0,1]}E\!\left[ \max_{0<c\leq M(k,s,\Psi,\theta)} \{u(c)+\beta J(M(k,s,\Psi,\theta)-c)\} \right]. \]

Require \(J\) to be finite and continuous on compact capital intervals. Define \(q_J(m)=\max_{0<c\leq m}\{u(c)+\beta J(m-c)\}\) and impose §1.2's portfolio integration, continuity, and measurable-selection conditions with continuation \(v=q_J\). These assumptions concern the composed functions and do not follow from matching domains.

Both period definitions discount once. They have different arrival information, state domains, and terminal-value interpretations; their finite-horizon value operators are not equal. Changing the stage list alone cannot change the economic order. The changed within-period connector and inter-period boundary make this second definition different. Exchanging expectation and consumption maximization would change what consumption observes. Trellises states the terminal domains for each definition.

docs.title: 4 Constructing a period
docs.text:
A period is a dictionary of records: {"stages": {key: record}, "connectors": [...]}, with one record for each stage occurrence. A record holds the stage source, its text and origin, and the three specification mappings the occurrence is bound with; bellman.stage.load_stage reads a stage file into a record whose three mappings are empty:

from bellman.stage import load_stage

record = load_stage("cons.bl")
# {"stage": {"text": ..., "origin": "cons.bl"}, "calibration": {}, "settings": {},
#  "methods": {"methods": []}, "provenance": {...}}

The application completes the three mappings and places the period in a trellis, since no call elaborates a period on its own. Either it appends the period with bellman.trellis.accrete(trellis, period, inter_connector=None), the terminal period first and each earlier period after it with the mapping that joins them, starting from {"periods": [], "inter_connectors": []}; or it writes the period into the periods list of a trellis dictionary, {"periods": [period], "inter_connectors": []}. Elaboration then constructs each distinct stage text once and returns the same dictionary with a constructed stage occurrence at each key, deriving the joins of the period from the fields as §3 describes, and the three trellis verbs, bellman.trellis.calibrate_trellis, bellman.trellis.methodize_trellis and bellman.trellis.configure_trellis, each given the elaborated trellis and the dictionary of records it came from, bind the three mappings in that order. The four stopping points, the symbolic trellis and the trellis after each verb, are the results of those four calls. A period may equally be built from stages already elaborated and bound one by one, bellman.stage.elaborate_stage(bellman.stage.load_stage(path)) followed by the stage's own calibrate, methodize and configure, and appended by accrete; a trellis verb later copies such a stage occurrence as it stands. The period is a dictionary of records before elaboration and a dictionary of constructed occurrences after it; nothing before the elaborator parses or rewrites a stage file.

The records of every period of a model are written at once by bellman.trellis.load_trellis(file), from a trellis file whose periods write their stages as records, or by bellman.trellis.load_recipe(directory, recipe), from a registry and its recipe; The Bellman factory is the route through those calls, and Period functions states accrete.

Elaboration takes a trellis, not a period

bellman.trellis.elaborate_trellis refuses a bare period. Place the period in a trellis, by accrete or as {"periods": [period], "inter_connectors": []}, and elaborate the trellis, as the trellis page shows. No stage-dependency graph is stored: the joins of a period and the order of its stages are derived from the selected connections. Construction records a cycle as a diagnostic; requesting a stage order for that cycle raises an error. Read the connection report to inspect unresolved or incompatible connections.

None of these calls solves the model.

docs.title: 5 Independent stage occurrences
docs.text:
Two uses of cons.bl may share source text, but each constructed stage occurrence is a separate object with its own graphs and its own specification, and the two share no object. What the stages of one period do share is the parameters they declare under one name: β declared in two stages of a period is one parameter of the period, whose declared sets must agree and which the period's calibration sources supply once, each declaring stage then binding that value (The trellis factory §4). A calibration change in one period does not alter another, since the same spelling in another period is another parameter, and no stage occurrence is adjusted in place. Reusing a stage file or caching its parse therefore does not justify sharing mutable stage annotations.

If a stage file occurs twice inside one period, give the two uses distinct keys and supply a source entry for each. Distinct keys identify the occurrences; their field interfaces must still make every join unambiguous. Across periods, the same local key may recur because the period index distinguishes its uses. The application evaluates a parameter schedule for each index when assembling that occurrence's record.

docs.title: Trellis Syntax
docs.text:
#trellis

Summary

A trellis is the sequence of a model's periods, counted backward from the terminal period, together with the connectors that join each period to the one after it in time. Three files describe it in the route a recipe reads, and the first two suffice when the periods carry their own records (§3). The trellis file lists the periods and the connectors between them; the period file is the template of one period, which the trellis file repeats; and the recipe names the trellis file and, for every stage key those two files use, the stage's file and the files of its parameter values, settings and methods, each by a path written from the recipe's own folder. This page explains how a trellis is loaded as it is written: what each file holds and what it leaves to the others, how periods are written out or repeated, where the files' paths are read from, and how the same trellis is built in Python one period at a time with no file at all. What a recipe does with the files it names, the order of its sources and the values supplied at the call, is the subject of the page that follows.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Periods: stage occurrences, connectors and the order of a period from its fields. Used by — The Bellman factory: the recipe route in full, from these files to a trellis whose every stage holds its values, methods and settings; Recipe functions and The trellis factory: the calls that read the files and what they return. See also — Model directory layout: where the files of a model stand. Formal account — Periods and the trellis: composition and boundary data.

Key terminology Term Meaning Trellis The sequence of a model's periods, periods[0] the terminal one, with the connectors between adjacent periods (wiki). Trellis file trellis.yml: the periods, each written out or given as a template repeated, and the inter-period connectors (§§1, 4). Period file period.yml: the template of one period, its stages and its connectors, which the trellis file names under template: (Periods; wiki). Recipe spec.yml: the trellis file under trellis: and, for each stage key, the stage's file and the files of its values, settings and methods, each by a path written from the recipe's folder; the file of the specification factory, the part of the Bellman factory that merges the sources a recipe names, which the next page explains (The Bellman factory; wiki). Stage key The name an author gives one use of a stage in a period, tenure; the recipe says which file it names. Stage occurrence One use of a stage file at one position of one period, an object of its own (Periods §1). Record The entry at one stage key of the syntactic trellis: the stage's text and origin and its three mappings, held as data (The factory API §2). Syntactic trellis The model as written, the dictionary of records that bellman.trellis.load_trellis and bellman.trellis.load_recipe return (wiki). Inter-period connector The mapping inter_connectors[h] from the continuation fields that leave periods[h + 1] to the arrival fields of periods[h] (wiki).

docs.title: 1 The three files
docs.text:
The preceding pages wrote one stage, and then one period. A model with a horizon uses several stages at many dates, and the durables model of the repository, applications/durables/, the housing model of Dobrescu and Shanker (2026) in which a household keeps or adjusts its housing stock at each of fifty-one ages, is the example of this page: four stage files, for the tenure choice, the keeper's consumption, the adjuster's consumption and the bequest, and three files that say how the stages are used. Each of the three answers one question, and none answers another's.

The trellis file, trellis.yml, composes. It lists the periods of the model, the terminal period first, and the connectors that join each period to the one after it in time. The durables file, with its comment lines left out:

!trellis
name: durables_life_cycle
periods:
  - stages: [tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons, bequest]
    connectors:
      - {a_nxt_kp: a_bq, h_nxt_kp: h_bq, z_nxt_kp: z_bq, a_nxt_adj: a_bq, h_nxt_adj: h_bq, z_nxt_adj: z_bq}
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
  - {template: period.yml, repeat: 50}
inter_connectors:
  - {a_nxt_kp: a, h_nxt_kp: h, z_nxt_kp: z, a_nxt_adj: a, h_nxt_adj: h, z_nxt_adj: z}

Its first entry writes the terminal period out, because that period alone holds the bequest and the connector that carries the savings, the housing and the income state of both consumption stages onto the bequest's arrival fields, and the template's connector after it, which joins the tenure stage's branches to the consumption stages; its second entry gives the fifty earlier periods as one template repeated. The one mapping under inter_connectors stands for every adjacent pair, and joins the continuation fields of both consumption stages to the arrival fields a, h and z of the next period's tenure stage.

The period file, period.yml, is a template: one period, written once and repeated by the trellis file under template:. It lists the keys of the stages the period holds and the connectors within the period. The order of its list carries no meaning, since the order of the stages is derived from their fields (Periods §3). Its one connector joins the fields each branch of the tenure stage ends at to the decision states of the consumption stage the branch enters, each consumption stage beginning at its decision perch; z_d, which both consumption stages read, is written with its stage key:

!period
name: durables_period
stages:
  - tenure
  - keeper_cons
  - adjuster_cons
connectors:
  - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}

The recipe, spec.yml, names the files. At its top it names the trellis file under trellis:, and for each stage key the two files above use it names the stage's file under stage: and the files whose values the stage receives, each by a path written from the recipe's own folder. What the recipe does with those files, the order of its lists, the entries written $fill and $tenure_method, the registry block and the bequest's periods: [0, 0], is the subject of The Bellman factory §3; on this page the recipe is read for what it names. The durables recipe, with its comment lines left out:

trellis: trellis.yml
stages:
  tenure:        {stage: stages/tenure/tenure.bl,               calibration: {all: [calibration/durables, $fill]}, settings: {all: [settings/durables, $fill]}, methods: {all: [stages/tenure/methods, $tenure_method]}}
  keeper_cons:   {stage: stages/keeper_cons/keeper_cons.bl,     calibration: {all: [calibration/durables, $fill]}, settings: {all: [settings/durables, $fill]}, methods: {all: [stages/keeper_cons/methods, $keeper_method]}}
  adjuster_cons: {stage: stages/adjuster_cons/adjuster_cons.bl, calibration: {all: [calibration/durables, $fill]}, settings: {all: [settings/durables, $fill]}, methods: {all: [stages/adjuster_cons/methods, $adjuster_method]}}
  bequest:       {stage: stages/bequest/bequest.bl,             calibration: {all: [calibration/durables, $fill]}, methods: {all: [stages/bequest/methods]}, periods: [0, 0]}
registry:
  calibration: [calibration/wage_schedule]

The division of labor is strict. The trellis file and the period file hold stage keys, connectors and inter-period connectors, and the trellis file the path of the period file it repeats, under template:; they hold no value, no method, no setting and no stage file. Reading them tells the package which stages occur where and how their fields are joined, and tells it nothing about what any stage receives. A stage key is a name the author chooses; which file it names, and which files that stage is bound from, the recipe says, and the recipe in turn writes no connector and determines the sequence of periods only through the trellis file it names at its top. The recipe is the file of the specification factory, the part of the Bellman factory that merges the sources a recipe names, which the next page explains (wiki). The call bellman.trellis.load_recipe("applications/durables/declaration", "spec.yml") reads the three files and returns the syntactic trellis, one record per stage and period (§6). A recipe cannot make a trellis on its own: without the trellis file it names there is no list of periods to write records for.

docs.title: 1.1 Periods counted backward
docs.text:
The periods list is read with the terminal period first. periods[0] is the terminal period, the last in time, and periods[h] lies h periods before it, so that the durables trellis has fifty-one entries, periods[0] being age 70 and periods[50] age 20. The index h is the number of periods before the last, not an age and not a calendar date. A stage file carries no index: the same file is used at every position where its key appears, and each use is a separate stage occurrence with its own bindings (Periods §5).

The trellis is counted this way because it is built this way. Backward induction values a period from the value of the period after it, so the terminal period is the first the package needs and the first it appends: the readers of the files write the records in this order, and the calls that construct a trellis append its periods in this order, the terminal period first (§6). Counting from the terminal period, an earlier period appended changes no index already present. The terminal period keeps the index 0 whatever the horizon, so that whatever a file writes for it means the same in a model of three periods as in one of fifty-one, and the horizon is the number of periods the trellis file lists, and nothing else sets it.

Entry Economic time Backward computation periods[0] The terminal period. Uses the supplied terminal continuation data (§2). periods[1] One period before the terminal one. Uses the result for periods[0]. periods[h + 1] One period before periods[h]. Uses the result for periods[h].

docs.title: 2 Inter-period connectors
docs.text:
inter_connectors[h] pairs continuation state fields that leave periods[h + 1] with arrival state fields of periods[h]; the mapping is written in the forward economic direction, from the earlier period to the later one, even though value computation proceeds from periods[0] to periods[1]. The list holds one mapping for each adjacent pair, so that its length is one less than the number of periods. In a trellis file, a list of one mapping stands for every pair, as the durables file writes it, and an absent or empty list stands for empty mappings, periods not joined to one another; the readers expand the list, so the trellis they return holds one mapping per adjacent pair. Each repeated mapping is resolved against its own period pair: an endpoint unique in one pair can be ambiguous in another. A trellis written in Python (§6) holds that many mappings itself, and any other length, in a file or in Python, is refused with the number of mappings to write.

As within a period, a connector selects two stage-local fields and performs no interest, discounting, or unit conversion. A bare endpoint name must identify exactly one eligible use on its side of the period pair; prefix an ambiguous name with its stage key. The joined fields must be continuation fields that leave the earlier period in time, those that no join within that period reads. An arrival field may take several sources, within its period and from the period before, and its arrival measure, the distribution of the agents who arrive there, is the sum of the incoming measures: the retirement model's a_ret takes the workers who retire and the retirees of the period before. An empty mapping supplies no authored pair; it does not repair missing or incompatible boundary data.

The two period definitions of the preceding page leave different fields at their boundaries:

Period definition Within-period pair Inter-period pair Terminal continuation domain Consumption, discounting, investment {k_next: k} {m_next: m} Positive resources, \((0,\infty)\). Investment, consumption, discounting {m_next: m} {k_next: k} Nonnegative capital, \([0,\infty)\).

For the first definition, port.m_next of period h+1 supplies cons.m of period h. For the second, disc.k_next supplies port.k. Each pairing requires compatible declared sets and the author's economic justification for the quantity, units and information. Use the matching within-period and inter-period choices together; reversing a stage list does not move a boundary.

The terminal continuation value is the value function that a stage of the terminal period reads after its decisions. Keep its input explicit: declare V[>] in the backward block's input header, including when the terminal payoff is given in closed form. You supply the function on the declared continuation-state domain. It may be identically zero, as in the durables model's bequest stage, but death, exit or the end of the horizon does not set it to zero automatically. A zero value does not require removing the continuation-state fields.

Supply this function as terminal data when the model is realized; no entry of inter_connectors is reserved for it. For the value-only stage files of the preceding page, use the domain in the table and the analytic conditions in Periods. A constant zero terminal value is admissible for those equations. Terminal data for a continuation given in closed form must also carry the derivatives that the blocks of the stage reading it name by their terms, D_{a}V[>], agreeing with the supplied value function (§2.1). The join rule above prescribes no representation for terminal data.

In a retirement model, a connector for one adjacent period pair must contain both routes when both are needed: working continuation fields connect to the next working or choice stage, and retired continuation fields connect to the next retired stage. Writing the two routes as separate entries of inter_connectors would assign them to different period joins. Retirement is absorbing only if the retired route continues to exclude a return to working stages.

docs.title: 2.1 The derivative a method reads
docs.text:
A block that a method binds, such as the block of !egm (Method types), may read the derivative of its stage's continuation value by the term D_{a}V[>] (Field equations §2). The block declares that reading and nothing else: how the derivative is evaluated is a property of the value, fixed by the stage that supplies the continuation, the stage whose exported value a connector joins to this stage's continuation fields (Methodization §4.1). That stage's value carries the derivative when its methods file fixed one, in one of two ways. The first is a derivative line, in its stage file or in a marginal block bound with !marginals, whose values the representation at the value builder's Evaluation stores; the methods file writes that representation at <block-id>.evaluate.value or <block-id>.evaluate.marginal. The second is a representation of the value whose row of the method table evaluates the derivative. A derivative line stated at the decision builder serves the arrival value through an arrival builder whose law between the perches is the identity, V[<] = V or V[<] = E_{y}V, where the stored derivative values pass through. Where that stage's derivative line in turn reads the derivative of the stage after it, as the portfolio stage's line reads D_{m_next}V[>] under its expectation, the requirement passes to that stage, and so on up to a stage whose continuation is given in closed form, such as the terminal continuation, whose derivatives are supplied with the terminal data (§2). The join of two stages compares value fields alone, and a connector selects values alone.

A reading that no route meets is reported, not refused: the trellis is built and bound, and the route that needs the derivative is left uncertified. bellman.trellis.derivative_missing(trellis) answers one derivative-missing diagnostic for each such reading, addressed to the stage occurrence whose value carries no derivative in the coordinate read, such as periods[0].stages['port']; its sentence names that stage, the value and the coordinate, as the reading block's term writes them, D_{m_next}V[>], and the ways the stage's methods file may fix the derivative. When every value carries the derivatives its neighbors read, the query answers an empty tuple.

docs.title: 3 The two shapes of a period
docs.text:
A period's stages: takes one of two shapes, and the shape decides which call reads the file and where the bindings come from.

Written as a list of keys, stages: [tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons], a period names its stages and binds nothing. This is the shape of the durables files of §1 and of every period a recipe reads: bellman.trellis.load_recipe(directory, "spec.yml") reads the trellis file through the recipe, which supplies for each key the stage's file and its three mappings. Without a recipe a list of keys cannot be read, since nothing says which file a key names; and under a recipe a period of records is refused, the refusal saying that under a recipe a period template lists its stage keys and the recipe supplies their mappings.

Written as a mapping from each key to a record, a period carries its own bindings and needs no recipe. Each record names the stage's file under stage:, which is required, and gives its calibration, its settings and its methods, each either inline as a mapping or as the path of a file, each of the three optional and empty when left out; every path is read relative to the trellis file's own folder, and a label may name the occurrence. bellman.trellis.load_trellis(file) reads such a file. The terminal period of the durables model and one period before it, written in this shape and read by that call:

!trellis
name: durables_records
periods:
  - stages:
      tenure:        {stage: stages/tenure/tenure.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/tenure/methods.yml}
      keeper_cons:   {stage: stages/keeper_cons/keeper_cons.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/keeper_cons/methods.yml}
      adjuster_cons: {stage: stages/adjuster_cons/adjuster_cons.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/adjuster_cons/methods.yml}
      bequest:       {stage: stages/bequest/bequest.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, methods: stages/bequest/methods.yml}
    connectors:
      - {a_nxt_kp: a_bq, h_nxt_kp: h_bq, z_nxt_kp: z_bq, a_nxt_adj: a_bq, h_nxt_adj: h_bq, z_nxt_adj: z_bq}
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
  - stages:
      tenure:        {stage: stages/tenure/tenure.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/tenure/methods.yml}
      keeper_cons:   {stage: stages/keeper_cons/keeper_cons.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/keeper_cons/methods.yml}
      adjuster_cons: {stage: stages/adjuster_cons/adjuster_cons.bl, calibration: calibration/durables.yml, settings: settings/durables.yml, methods: stages/adjuster_cons/methods.yml}
    connectors:
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
inter_connectors:
  - {a_nxt_kp: a, h_nxt_kp: h, z_nxt_kp: z, a_nxt_adj: a, h_nxt_adj: h, z_nxt_adj: z}

The bequest's record names a calibration file and a methods file and no settings, so its settings are empty. A mapping written inline, settings: {n_a: 200}, stands where a path does. A record holds one source of each kind and nothing more, so that a value which differs by period is written in this route directly, each period's records naming their own files; what a recipe writes instead is the subject of The Bellman factory §3. The trellis files of records of applications/cons-port/declaration/, trellis.port-cons-vfi.yml and the five trellis.reference-<name>.yml of its fixed reference, are written in this shape, each stage: path naming a stage file of the folder's own stages/.

In this route the tenure record of each period gives a calibration, a file or an inline mapping, that holds that period's income Y and retirement income y_R beside the common values, since these vary with age and a record merges nothing; the fragment above names the common file in both periods, so bellman.trellis.load_trellis reads it and bellman.trellis.elaborate_trellis constructs it, but bellman.trellis.calibrate_trellis refuses it at Y.

The two shapes are told apart by the shape alone, a list or a mapping, and are not mixed: a file that writes one period as keys and another as records is refused by both calls, each naming the shape it reads. A stage entry of the second shape is a key with a record, never a key with a bare list of files. Either shape may stand in a period written out in the trellis file or in a period file named under template:, and whichever shape a model uses, the two calls return the same kind of dictionary, the syntactic trellis of §6, which the same calls then elaborate and bind.

docs.title: 4 Periods written out and repeated
docs.text:
The periods list is written entry by entry, and an entry is either a period written out or a template repeated.

A period written out is a mapping with stages and connectors, and a trellis file may write every period this way, one entry per period from the terminal period backward, with one inter-period mapping for each adjacent pair. The durables model with three periods, written out:

!trellis
name: durables_three_periods
periods:
  - stages: [tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons, bequest]
    connectors:
      - {a_nxt_kp: a_bq, h_nxt_kp: h_bq, z_nxt_kp: z_bq, a_nxt_adj: a_bq, h_nxt_adj: h_bq, z_nxt_adj: z_bq}
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
  - stages: [tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons]
    connectors:
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
  - stages: [tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons]
    connectors:
      - {w_kp: w_d, h_kp: h_d, z_kp: keeper_cons.z_d, w_adj: m, z_adj: adjuster_cons.z_d}
inter_connectors:
  - {a_nxt_kp: a, h_nxt_kp: h, z_nxt_kp: z, a_nxt_adj: a, h_nxt_adj: h, z_nxt_adj: z}
  - {a_nxt_kp: a, h_nxt_kp: h, z_nxt_kp: z, a_nxt_adj: a, h_nxt_adj: h, z_nxt_adj: z}

Read through the durables recipe, this file gives three periods and two inter-period connectors, and since the two mappings are equal the list may be written as one mapping standing for both pairs.

A period repeated is the entry {template: <period file>, repeat: n}: the period file, read relative to the trellis file's folder, is expanded to n equal periods, n a positive integer and one when repeat is left out. A period written out may carry repeat as well, and the three trellis files of the cons-port application each write one period of records with repeat: 6.

The two kinds of entry stand in one list, which is how the periods that differ are written out and the rest repeated. The durables file of §1 writes the terminal period out and repeats the template fifty times; a first period of life that differed from the others would be a third entry, written out after the template's. A template entry may also change what the template says, since the entry's own keys stand over the file's: an entry {template: period.yml, repeat: 2, connectors: [...]} repeats the template with the connectors it writes in place of the file's. Whatever the entries, the readers expand them, so the trellis they return holds one entry per period and one mapping per adjacent pair, and periods[h] is read as §1 counts it.

docs.title: 5 The recipe's paths and variants side by side
docs.text:
A recipe names every file it reads by a path relative to its own folder, and it assumes nothing from a name or a layout. At its top, trellis: trellis.yml names the trellis file; in each stage entry, stage: stages/tenure/tenure.bl names the stage's file; and in the lists of files a stage receives, calibration/durables names a calibration file without its extension, .yml or .yaml. Both trellis: and stage: are required. A recipe without the first, or an entry without the second, is refused with the sentence that shows what to write (Refusals), and no file is found from a stage key's spelling. The recipe's folder, the one the first argument of bellman.trellis.load_recipe(directory, "spec.yml") names, is therefore the one place every path of the recipe is read from, and how that folder is arranged is a convention of the model, not a rule of the reader (Model directory layout).

The trellis file resolves its own names the same way, relative to its own folder: the period file under template: and, in the records route, every stage: and every path of a record (§3). A trellis file beside its recipe therefore reads the same stages/ folder, and the cons-port files reach stage files two folders up with ../../portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/port/port.bl.

A second route through the same stages, a variant, is written as a second set of the three files beside the first and nothing else: spec.<name>.yml, trellis.<name>.yml and period.<name>.yml, the name between the dots chosen by the author. The variant recipe names its trellis file under trellis:, that file names its template under template:, and both share the stage files and the source files of the folder, so that the suffix is for the eye alone, every link between the three files being written in the files. The durables folder keeps its route without the tenure stage this way, as spec.two-stages.yml, trellis.two-stages.yml and period.two-stages.yml, and bellman.trellis.load_recipe("applications/durables/declaration", "spec.two-stages.yml") opens it. A variant that changes the values a stage receives and not the route needs no second set of files; how a recipe writes it is the subject of The Bellman factory §3.

docs.title: 6 A trellis built in Python
docs.text:
Every route ends in the same dictionary, and the dictionary can be written without any file. A trellis is {"periods": [...], "inter_connectors": [...]}, each period {"stages": {key: record}, "connectors": [...]}, and a record is what bellman.stage.load_stage(path) returns: the stage's text and origin under stage, its calibration, settings and methods empty, and its provenance; the application completes the three mappings (Periods §4; The factory API §2). A record may also be written from text, {"stage": {"text": source_text, "origin": producer}, "calibration": {}, "settings": {}, "methods": {}}, since elaboration reads no file; a path string in place of a record is refused.

bellman.trellis.accrete(trellis, period, inter_connector=None) appends one period, the one earlier in time, to a trellis that starts as {"periods": [], "inter_connectors": []}. The terminal period is appended first and takes no mapping; each earlier period is appended with the mapping that joins it to the period appended before it, which accrete writes at inter_connectors[len(periods) - 2]. The durables model with three periods, built this way from records and then elaborated, run from the repository root:

from bellman.stage import load_stage
from bellman.trellis import accrete, elaborate_trellis

folder = "applications/durables/declaration"

def record(name):
    """The record of one durables stage file, its three mappings empty."""
    return load_stage(f"{folder}/stages/{name}/{name}.bl")

decisions = {"tenure": record("tenure"), "keeper_cons": record("keeper_cons"), "adjuster_cons": record("adjuster_cons")}
to_bequest = {"a_nxt_kp": "a_bq", "h_nxt_kp": "h_bq", "z_nxt_kp": "z_bq", "a_nxt_adj": "a_bq", "h_nxt_adj": "h_bq", "z_nxt_adj": "z_bq"}
to_tenure = {"a_nxt_kp": "a", "h_nxt_kp": "h", "z_nxt_kp": "z", "a_nxt_adj": "a", "h_nxt_adj": "h", "z_nxt_adj": "z"}

trellis = {"periods": [], "inter_connectors": []}
trellis = accrete(trellis, {"stages": {**decisions, "bequest": record("bequest")}, "connectors": [to_bequest]})
trellis = accrete(trellis, {"stages": decisions, "connectors": []}, to_tenure)
trellis = accrete(trellis, {"stages": decisions, "connectors": []}, to_tenure)
symbolic = elaborate_trellis(trellis)
for h, period in enumerate(symbolic["periods"]):
    print(f"periods[{h}]:", ", ".join(period["stages"]))
print(len(symbolic["inter_connectors"]), "inter-period connectors;", repr(symbolic["periods"][2]["stages"]["tenure"]))

periods[0]: tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons, bequest
periods[1]: tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons
periods[2]: tenure, keeper_cons, adjuster_cons
2 inter-period connectors; ElaboratedStage('tenure', symbolic)

The same records are given to all three periods, and elaboration still constructs a separate stage occurrence at each position, each carrying its position in its provenance, since accrete copies what it appends and the elaborator places a full copy of each stage at each of its positions. bellman.trellis.elaborate_trellis constructs each distinct stage text once, selects the connections of each period and checks each inter-period mapping, retaining representable connection problems on the returned model for inspection through the connection report; it binds nothing, so the calibration, settings and methods stand in the records as data. bellman.trellis.calibrate_trellis, bellman.trellis.methodize_trellis and bellman.trellis.configure_trellis, each given the elaborated trellis and the dictionary of records, then bind the three mappings in that order, and the four results, the symbolic trellis and the trellis after each verb, are the four stopping points of the construction (The trellis factory §§3, 4). A period whose stages are already elaborated, each by bellman.stage.elaborate_stage(bellman.stage.load_stage(path)) and bound by the stage's own verbs, is appended in the same way and its joins are derived at once; a trellis verb later copies such a stage occurrence as it stands (Period functions §3). A bare period is not elaborated on its own: it is placed in a trellis first, by accrete or as {"periods": [period], "inter_connectors": []} (Periods §4).

The syntactic trellis that bellman.trellis.load_recipe or bellman.trellis.load_trellis returns from the files of §§1 and 3 is a dictionary of this same form, and the same four calls elaborate and bind it; bellman.trellis.assemble_trellis("applications/durables/declaration", "spec.yml") runs the whole route in one call (The Bellman factory §2). The result of every call is a dictionary of periods and inter_connectors, beside which a reader writes the provenance of the files it read and bellman.trellis.load_recipe the recipe's registry-level names (The Bellman factory §3.5), the later calls copying both; no graph is stored: the joins are derived from the fields when the trellis is elaborated, and bellman.trellis.diagram_trellis(trellis) draws the periods with their inter-period connectors on request (The trellis factory §6).

docs.title: The Bellman factory
docs.text:
Summary

The Bellman factory is the part of the package that takes a model from its files to a trellis whose every stage holds its values, methods and settings. The preceding page explains how a trellis is loaded as it is written; this page is the recipe route in full.
